summary: The publish workflow now supports a manual trigger with an option to publish exclusively to Test PyPI. This change removes the requirement for a specific deployment environment and updates action versions.

This commit improves file upload handling by automatically inferring filenames from file-like objects. The new `guess_filename` utility extracts the name attribute if it is not a placeholder, and `Request.send` now uses this to set the filename in multipart fields.

This commit updates the installation documentation to clarify that the guide specifically covers the Requests library. The change modifies the main heading in the user installation guide to explicitly name the software.
This commit adds a link to the Spanish translation of the documentation in the sidebar. It updates the sidebarintro.html template to include the new language option for users.
This commit adds support for the HTTP PATCH method to the requests library. It updates the `request` function in `requests/api.py` to accept PATCH requests and exports the new `patch` function.

The test `test_mixed_case_scheme_acceptable` in `test_requests.py` now uses the local `HTTPBIN_URL` variable instead of hard-coded external URLs. This change ensures the test for mixed-case URL schemes runs reliably against the local test server.

This commit fixes an issue where mixed-case URL schemes prevented effective connection pooling. The HTTPAdapter class now lowercases URLs before passing them to the underlying pool manager. Tests were added to verify that mixed-case schemes are handled correctly.

This commit fixes a type mismatch error in the `MockRequest` class within `requests/cookies.py`. It ensures that when the host header is patched into a URL, the host is converted to a string if the parsed URL components are strings, preventing crashes from mixing bytes and text types.

This commit updates the project history to record the release of version 0.6.4. It also corrects a typo in the changelog, changing the reference to the advanced response interface from "r.fo" to "r.faw".

This commit updates documentation links to use HTTPS instead of HTTP for improved security. It modifies the README and various documentation files to ensure all references to GitHub, PyPI, and Read the Docs use secure connections.

The `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py` now correctly handles the `prefetch` parameter when explicitly set to `False`. Previously, passing `False` did not override the request's default prefetch setting, causing unexpected behavior. This change ensures the parameter properly controls whether the response is prefetched.

This commit corrects spelling errors in the project documentation and source code comments. It fixes typos in the HTTPProxyAuth class and the RequestEncodingMixin module, improving the accuracy of the user-facing text.
This commit corrects a typo in the advanced user documentation. It fixes a misspelled variable name in an example, ensuring the text accurately reflects the correct spelling.

This commit modifies the `Request` class in `requests/models.py` to use weak references when linking a request to its response. This change prevents circular references between the two objects, which helps the garbage collector free memory more efficiently.
This commit adds a new license image file to the extension directory. It introduces the visual asset required for displaying license information within the application.

This commit introduces a new setup.py file to configure the packaging and distribution of the requests library. It defines the package metadata, dependencies, and includes a helper function to publish the project to PyPI.

This commit removes a redundant conditional check for cookies within the `Request.send` method in `requests/models.py`. The change cleans up the code by eliminating a block that performed no action, leaving only a commented-out reference.

This commit fixes a Python 2 compatibility issue in the requests library by ensuring the `str` alias is correctly defined within the `compat` module. It resolves a potential error where the alias was missing or incorrectly placed, ensuring consistent behavior for string handling in older Python versions.

This commit refactors the Session class in requests/sessions.py to improve code readability. It consolidates the request method's parameter list into a more compact format and adjusts comment spacing. No functional behavior changes are introduced.

This commit updates the project's README documentation to clarify that connection pooling is provided by the urllib3 library. It removes the statement that urllib3 is embedded within the Requests module, correcting the description of the dependency relationship.

This commit reorders the arguments in the `HTTPAdapter` initialization method to prevent breaking changes for existing users. By moving the `pool_block` parameter to the end of the argument list, the function maintains backward compatibility with code that relies on the previous positional argument order.

This commit adds documentation for a new `prefetch` parameter in the `request` function within `requests/api.py`. It clarifies that setting this option to true immediately downloads the response content, allowing users to control when data is fetched.

This commit updates the project title in the README file to include decorative emoji characters. It adjusts the underline length to match the new title width, ensuring the documentation header renders correctly.

This commit corrects a typo in the project's dependency list by replacing the invalid package name "pytestt" with the correct "pytest". This ensures the testing framework installs properly during environment setup.

The `Response.json` method in `requests/models.py` now uses `complexjson` instead of the standard `json` module for parsing. This ensures consistent JSON decoding behavior across different Python environments.
Adds a new flake8 target to the Makefile that runs the linter while ignoring line length errors. This allows developers to easily check code style compliance from the command line.

The `unquote_unreserved` function in `requests/utils.py` is rewritten to handle invalid percent-encodings gracefully instead of crashing. This change makes the URL decoding process more robust and simplifies the underlying code logic.

This commit updates the bundled CA certificate bundle in the requests library to version 2017.4.17. It removes the outdated RSA Security 2048 v3 certificate from the cacert.pem file, ensuring the library uses the current trusted root certificates for secure connections.

This commit improves the documentation for the `Session` class in the `requests` library. It adds detailed descriptions for instance attributes like headers, authentication, and timeouts, and includes the class in the API reference.

This commit updates the quickstart documentation to clarify that dictionary keys with a value of None are excluded from the URL query string when using the requests library. It addresses a potential confusion for users who expect all provided parameters to appear in the final request URL.

This commit adjusts the visual alignment of the sea turtle logo in the documentation layout. It adds a CSS style rule to the layout template to shift the image slightly to the left, correcting its positioning on the page.

This commit reverts the hooks functionality from a sub-package back to a single module within the requests library. It consolidates hook setup and dispatch logic into requests/hooks.py, removing the previous directory structure.

This commit removes the test suite for the asynchronous API in the requests library. It deletes the file containing tests for the async module, which is no longer supported. Users will no longer see these specific test cases run during the test suite.
This commit updates the project history to document a performance improvement in the CaseInsensitiveDict class. It notes that the dictionary now caches lower-case keys to optimize lookup operations.

This commit updates the packaging configuration in setup.py to explicitly include the requests.packages.urllib3.packages module. This ensures the nested dependency is correctly bundled when the package is installed.
Adds a new image asset named flourish.png to the extension directory. This file is likely used for visual branding or interface elements within the extension.

The `ok` property in the `Response` class now returns a boolean based on whether the status code is less than 400, rather than raising an exception. This change clarifies the method's contract and prevents unexpected errors when checking response status.

This commit updates internal imports in the auth, models, and sessions modules to reference the to_native_string function from the new _internal_utils module instead of the public utils module. This change reorganizes the codebase by moving internal helper functions to a dedicated private module.

This documentation update clarifies that the `params` argument in the Requests library expects a dictionary of strings. It corrects the quickstart guide to specify the required data type for URL query parameters.

This commit updates the documentation sidebar for the certifi project. It adds a link to the official Certifi website, allowing users to easily access the recommended CA bundle information from the project's documentation.
Adds a new default setting called `encode_urls` to the `requests` library's default configuration. This change enables URL encoding by default, affecting how requests handle URL components.

This commit updates the requests adapters module to import the basestring type from the compatibility layer. It ensures the module has access to this type for proper string handling across different Python versions.
The `header_expand` function in `requests/utils.py` now accepts Unicode strings by encoding them to Latin-1 bytes. This prevents errors when users pass Unicode header values directly to the library.

This commit updates the `Response.raise_for_status` method in the `requests` library to attach the response object to the raised `HTTPError` exception. This allows users to access the original response data directly from the exception instance when handling errors.

This commit updates the advanced user documentation to explain the request lifecycle. It clarifies that response bodies are downloaded lazily only when the content attribute is accessed, rather than immediately upon making the request.

This commit removes Python 3.3 support from the project's build and packaging configuration. It updates the CI pipelines and setup metadata to no longer test or declare compatibility with that version.

This commit removes the bundled Python 2.7 collections module from the urllib3 package. It eliminates the need for the vendored `__collections.py` file, which contained abstract base classes like Mapping and MutableMapping. This change simplifies the codebase by relying on the standard library's built-in collections.

This release introduces a new command-line utility, `python -m requests.help`, to assist users with debugging and troubleshooting. The version number in the `requests` module is updated to 2.16.4 to reflect this addition.

The Request class in requests/models.py now correctly handles URLs containing unencoded path characters. This ensures that paths are properly percent-encoded when constructing the final request URL, preventing potential parsing errors or malformed requests.

This commit updates the project documentation to replace a Twitter handle link with the plain name "Kenneth Reitz." It improves the readability of the text by removing the external hyperlink reference.

The Makefile now runs the full test suite instead of only the requests tests, adding color output for local runs. It also introduces a new server target to launch the httpbin application via gunicorn.

This commit introduces the chardet module as a replacement for the charade dependency within the requests package. It adds the necessary files and classes, such as the detect function, to handle character encoding detection. This change prepares the library to use chardet for identifying text encodings.

This release fixes a bug where the last line of a response was truncated during iteration. It also enforces safe mode for asynchronous requests and improves how exceptions are handled in that mode. The version number in the requests module was updated to 0.8.7.

This commit updates the documentation to reflect Twitter's increased character limit. It changes the recommended maximum length for support tweets from 140 to 280 characters in the community support guide.
This commit adds a `prefetch` option to the `request` function and `Session.request` method. When enabled, it immediately downloads the response content instead of waiting for the user to access it.

This commit updates the success message displayed by the Makefile after building the documentation. It changes the wording from "Installed!" to "Build successful!" to more accurately describe the action performed.

Adds a new `is_redirect` property to the `Response` class in the `requests` library. This property indicates whether the response status code represents a redirect that the library could process, regardless of whether the redirect was actually followed.
This commit updates the project's author list to include the urllib3 team. It adds Andrey Petrov as a development lead under a new urllib3 section in the AUTHORS file.

This commit updates the project's author list by renaming the "Development Lead" and "Core Contributors" sections to "Keepers of the Three Crystals." It also adds a specific title to Kenneth Reitz's entry.

This commit introduces a `merge_kwargs` function to the `requests/sessions.py` module, allowing the `Session` class to properly combine default and local keyword arguments. It ensures that `None` values in local arguments do not override existing defaults, improving the handling of session configuration parameters.

This commit removes the project's Makefile, which previously provided targets for running tests and managing dependencies. Users will no longer be able to use make commands to install packages or execute test suites.

This commit fixes the rendering of a list in the "Custom Headers" section of the quickstart documentation. It corrects the indentation in the quickstart.rst file to ensure the text displays properly as a list item.

This commit adds regression tests to verify that the requests library correctly handles binary data uploads. It introduces test cases in the RequestsTestSuite class to ensure that sending non-UTF-8 bytes and encoded strings does not cause errors.
This commit restores the ASCII art logo to the module docstring in `requests/__init__.py`. Users will see the familiar graphical banner when viewing the package documentation or help text.
This commit adds a promotional link for Requests stickers to the documentation sidebar. It updates the sidebar templates to display a "Stickers!" heading that directs users to an external store.

This commit updates the project documentation to clarify that HTTP response headers are returned as a case-insensitive dictionary. It also adds a new entry describing the Response.history attribute, which provides a list of responses for tracking redirections.
The lock-issues workflow now runs once daily instead of hourly, reducing unnecessary background activity. It also updates the lock-threads action to version 3.
The quickstart again uses GitHub's public timeline to demonstrate an HTTP GET. The examples in quickstart.rst update the request URL and sample response to match GitHub.

Requests now honors the ALL_PROXY environment variable when rebuilding proxy settings. SessionRedirectMixin.rebuild_proxies looks for an all-schemes proxy before the scheme-specific environment setting and preserves explicitly configured proxies.

Cookie dictionaries now work on Python 3 as well as Python 2. The cookiejar_from_dict helper avoids the Python 2-only iteritems method, and the cookie assertion helper uses a compatible way to iterate over keyword arguments.
The lint and test workflows now use version 5.4.0 of the GitHub Action that installs Python. The change updates actions/setup-python in lint.yml and run-tests.yml from version 5.3.0.
The changelog now records the addition of request timeouts. HISTORY.rst adds a section for version 0.3.3 with an entry for the feature.

Users can once again access urllib3, idna, and chardet as attributes of requests.packages. The packages module binds those imports to its namespace, and new tests check that each attribute is available.
The test suite now serves its local HTTP endpoints through Gunicorn. RequestsTestSuite.setUp connects to the httpbin application on the configured local test port.

A timed-out request in safe mode now produces an empty response when the exception is suppressed. Request.send initializes the response before sending, and a test covers timeout handling with and without safe mode.
The documentation sidebar now links the sponsor name to Linode's site and removes the old support form. The sidebarintro.html template moves the sponsorship acknowledgment into the introduction.

The upload tests now have clearer descriptions of the expected HTTP headers. The docstrings in TestRequests explain the Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding checks, including the case of a generator body.
Travis CI now runs the regular test target. The script in .travis.yml switches the build from the Makefile's coverage target to its test target.

HTTP Basic authentication no longer retries indefinitely on repeated authentication errors in Python 2.6.5. The custom _HTTPBasicAuthHandler in requests/core.py resets the retry counter once per request so repeated challenges can reach the retry limit.

The documentation for Response.close now explains what happens when a response is closed. The docstring in requests/models.py says the connection is returned to the pool and warns against accessing the underlying raw response afterward.

The advanced guide now shows how to defer downloading a response body using the stream option. The example in advanced.rst replaces the old prefetch setting and explains that accessing Response.content triggers the download.
The test suite now covers more of the CaseInsensitiveDict interface. TestCaseInsensitiveDict checks comparisons with unsupported objects, equality after copying, and the dictionary's representation.

The HTTP DELETE tests now check that optional arguments reach the shared request function. RequestsAPIUnitTests mocks requests.api.request and verifies that requests.delete forwards options such as headers, authentication, and timeouts.

The changelog begins documenting the Requests 2.0 release. HISTORY.rst adds a draft section for API changes, including native string header names and the requirement for explicit schemes in proxy URLs.
The project copyright year is updated to 2014. The change updates both the LICENSE file and the documentation settings in docs/conf.py.
This commit tidies whitespace around imports in the Requests source. It adjusts spacing in requests/async.py and requests/core.py as part of the cleanup.
The installation guide now points users to the Requests organization on GitHub. The clone command, source archive link, and download example in install.rst all use the new repository location.
The test suite now checks the headers used when a generator supplies an upload body. TestRequests adds a case that expects chunked transfer encoding without a Content-Length header.

The package is reorganized so the public HTTP helpers and request models live in dedicated modules. The new requests.api module exposes request, get, and the other verb helpers and imports Request and Response from requests.models.

Requests now warns users that older versions of cryptography can slow it down. The _check_cryptography helper in requests/__init__.py checks for versions earlier than 1.3.4, and the changelog records the warning.
The development guide updates its description of how Requests is managed. The management section in philosophy.rst includes the library's presentation among the project lead's responsibilities.
The Request.send docstring uses the correct capitalization for the False return value. The change is confined to the method's description in requests/models.py.
The development guide now explains how to set up and run the test suite with pytest. The instructions in todo.rst use the Makefile's test-deps target to install the test dependencies.

CI test runs now produce a JUnit XML report using nose's built-in reporting. The Makefile switches away from NoseXUnit and adds a separate target to collect Pyflakes output, while reqs.txt drops the unused reporting dependency.

Requests now handles timeouts through its usual request error path. Request.send catches urllib2 URL errors along with HTTP errors and converts a wrapped socket timeout to the Requests Timeout exception.

The response decoding helper now returns Unicode when it decodes content with a detected encoding. The change corrects get_unicode_from_response in requests/utils.py, which previously attempted to use str on that path.
The README adds a decorative cake and sparkle line to the installation example. The addition appears below the existing Requests installation command.
The development environment now allows pytest 9. The constraint in requirements-dev.txt raises the upper limit to versions below 10 while keeping the existing minimum version.

The request API documentation now explains how to submit repeated form field names. The data parameter docstring in requests.api.request describes passing a list of key-value tuples for form encoding.
The request tests now use updated endpoints for HTTPS and user-agent checks. RequestsTestSuite uses GitHub for the HTTPS example and httpbin to check that the supplied user-agent header is sent.
The documentation sidebar now links to Requests-Toolbelt. The sidebarintro.html template adds it to the related links and inserts a horizontal divider.
The Requests README now displays a GitHub contributor-count badge. The new badge links readers to the repository's contributors graph.

The advanced guide removes its description of chardet as a mandatory Python 2 dependency. It also corrects the Requests package name and the spelling of the optional chardet extra in the encoding section.
Pytest now runs the examples included in Requests module docstrings. The change enables module doctests in pytest.ini and fixes examples in modules such as requests.api and requests.utils.
HTTPAdapter.send changes how it re-raises a caught exception. The adapters module now raises the captured exception object explicitly.
A plain IPv4 address in no_proxy can now bypass the proxy. The should_bypass_proxies helper in requests/utils.py compares the address directly when the entry is outside CIDR notation.
This commit makes a whitespace cleanup in the Request class. It inserts blank lines around declarations in requests/models.py.
The API documentation now shows how to configure Requests logging. The commit also adds Sphinx to setup.py for documentation builds and ignores build output and egg files in .gitignore.

This commit reorganizes part of the request-sending implementation. Request.send replaces old commented-out connection code with placeholder branches for files, data, and cookies and adds a comment about resending requests.

This commit cleans up the documentation presentation and adds internationalization wrappers. It changes the Sphinx sidebar templates and configuration and removes most of the previous custom stylesheet.
The test suite now covers sessions that use a standard CookieJar. RequestsTestCase initializes a cookielib.CookieJar with a cookie and exercises it as the session's cookie storage.
The README revises the tagline that describes Requests. The new wording presents it as a simple and elegant HTTP library.
This commit prepares Requests version 2.8.1. It records the release in HISTORY.rst and updates the version and build identifiers in requests/__init__.py.

The test suite now checks that users can configure the number of request retries. RequestsTestCase.test_can_specify_retries wraps the connection pool's urlopen method to record the retry settings it receives.
The README's HTTP Basic authentication example is now valid Python. The requests.get example supplies the URL as a quoted string.
The installation guide now recommends cloning Requests over HTTPS. The Git command in install.rst uses an HTTPS GitHub URL in place of the git protocol.
The changelog records that Requests 0.11.1 follows POST redirects with a GET by default. The new HISTORY.rst entry also describes the strict_mode option for disabling that behavior.
The Session.request docstring now documents the stream option and its default. It removes descriptions of the old return_response, config, and prefetch arguments.

Running the setup test command on a fresh environment no longer imports Requests just to obtain its version. Setup.py reads the version from requests/__init__.py, avoiding the vendored import hook left behind by the earlier setup process.
The quickstart now explains when a custom Authorization header is overridden. It names credentials supplied through the auth argument and credentials available through a .netrc file.
The advanced guide adds a note about keeping a connection open. Its keep-alive section explains that callers may need to set the Connection header manually.

Requests now registers its vendored import alias ahead of other import hooks. The VendorAlias registration in requests.packages gives it priority so Python 2 can fall back to built-in imports correctly.
The response hook test now sends a prepared request so the hook actually runs. TestRequests.test_hook_receives_request_arguments uses a Session to exercise the registered hook.
Streaming a response no longer prints every chunk as debug output. Response.iter_content drops the temporary generator that printed each item before yielding it.
The project now spells Google App Engine consistently. The change corrects the development guide and a compatibility comment in get_netrc_auth.

The documentation clarifies which types callers should use for HTTP header values. The API guide and quickstart describe string values and explain the distinction between native header names and permitted value types.

The HTTP PATCH tests now check that optional arguments reach the common request function. RequestsAPIUnitTests mocks requests.api.request and checks forwarding of data, headers, and other keyword arguments.
The README adds a spacer below the project attribution and support text. The change inserts an empty paragraph in that part of the Markdown file.
This commit makes an import compatibility fix for Python 2.5. The vendored oreos package initializer imports dict_from_string explicitly from its core module.

Cookie handling now calls the compatibility URL parser correctly when reading the request's scheme and host. MockRequest in requests/cookies.py uses urlparse directly, including the code path exercised by secure cookies.
Requests corrects how it starts tracking redirect history. Request._build_response limits that step to a redirect response on a request that is not already marked as redirected.
The documentation's sea turtle logo now displays the tattoos page URL in its title text. The change updates the logo image in the sidebarintro.html and sidebarlogo.html templates.
This commit removes an unused import from the certificate bundle module. The cleanup drops os.path from requests/certs.py.
The documentation sidebar now labels its support section Get Support. The sidebar templates replace the old Donate heading and remove the donation markup beneath it.
The advanced guide removes its advice about manually setting a keep-alive header for older servers. This reverts the connection keep-alive documentation change in advanced.rst.

The documentation homepage reorganizes its testimonials and download information. The monthly download figure moves out of the testimonials text and appears after the list of organizations using Requests.
The project credits Jérémy Bethmont as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
Requests can fall back to the distribution's CA certificates when the packaged bundle file is absent. The certificate lookup in requests/utils.py only sets the Certifi bundle path if the file exists.
Request authentication is now set through the shared authentication dispatcher. The Request class in requests/models.py delegates to requests.auth as part of removing AuthObject.
The Response.reason attribute is now declared as a string for type checkers. The Response initializer in requests/models.py retains its initial None value with an explicit type-checker suppression.
This commit cleans up the Requests packaging script. The change is in setup.py.
The quickstart now shows how to submit multiple form values under the same key. Its POST examples demonstrate passing a list of tuples through the data argument.
The project notice removes an extra blank line at the end. The change adjusts the formatting of the NOTICE file.

Users can configure proxies for Requests through environment variables. The Request class and the advanced guide add support and examples for HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY alongside per-request proxy settings.
The project credits Vikram Oberoi as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and GitHub handle under Patches and Suggestions.
The request implementation now imports its multipart upload helpers from the installed poster package. The imports in requests/core.py use poster's encoding and streaming HTTP modules directly.

Proxy bypass checks no longer include credentials in hostname matching or DNS lookup. The should_bypass_proxies helper in requests/utils.py uses the parsed hostname, addressing DNS failures noted on macOS.
The packaging script now reads the README and release history as UTF-8. Setup.py uses an explicit encoding when loading README.rst and HISTORY.rst for package metadata.
MockRequest now exposes its unverifiable flag as a property. The property in requests/cookies.py delegates to is_unverifiable in place of the dynamic attribute lookup.
This commit fixes spelling mistakes across the changelog, modules, and tests. The corrections include proxy environment variable text, cookie helper comments, and the name of a session hook test.
The request code now notes that handling connection-refused errors from urllib remains to be implemented. The note is added to Request.send in requests/models.py.

Concurrent extraction of a file from a ZIP archive no longer races to create the same directory hierarchy. The extract_zipped_paths helper reads the member and writes it atomically to a flat temporary path.

The project adds Python 3.10 to its test and packaging configuration. The test workflow includes a 3.10 development build, setup.py declares 3.10 support, and the development pytest constraint is raised.
URLs with leading or trailing whitespace are now cleaned up before parsing. PreparedRequest.prepare_url strips both ends of the input, and a regression test checks this behavior.
The FAQ fixes an apostrophe typo in its description of automatic response decoding. The correction is in the community documentation's discussion of gzip and Unicode.
Tests no longer inherit proxy settings from the caller's environment. The clean_proxy_environ fixture in tests/conftest.py clears the HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, all-proxy, and bypass variables for each test.
The README updates the introductory tagline for Requests. The new text describes the project as handcrafted for the Python community.
The documentation sidebar simplifies its list of project links. The sidebarintro.html template drops the Flattr and Stack Overflow entries and moves the PyPI entry.
The Requests source distribution now includes its Python test files. MANIFEST.in recursively adds the contents of the tests directory that match Python files.
The README describes the download count as approximately 60 million. The change revises the wording of the project's popularity statement.
The requests.packages namespace again makes bundled dependency names available. The restored packages.py module imports chardet, urllib3, and idna.
Chunked uploads now use urllib3's built-in chunking support. HTTPAdapter.send delegates this work to urllib3, replacing a separate code path for chunked requests.
Preparing a request without any hooks now passes an empty list to the hook preparation step. The change in PreparedRequest.prepare addresses the failing Unicode URL preparation test.
Travis CI no longer includes the Python 3.7 development build in its active test matrix. The change comments out that entry in .travis.yml to speed up CI runs.
A permanent redirect to the same URL is no longer saved in the redirect cache. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects checks that the target and original URLs differ before caching the redirect.
Hooks added by authentication now reach request hook dispatch. Session.request merges the prepared request's hooks into the original hooks dictionary before dispatch.
The publication workflow now uses version 7.0.0 of the upload-artifact GitHub Action. The change updates the action reference in publish.yml from version 6.0.0.

Stored authentication can now be found for a request on the same domain with a matching path. AuthManager.get_auth searches the stored entries, and add_auth attempts to convert incoming credentials to an AuthObject.
The project credits Johan Bergström as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name to the list of patches and suggestions.
The Requests package version is bumped to 1.0.4. The change updates both the version and build identifiers in requests/__init__.py.
The response prefetch tests now work with byte strings on Python 3. RequestsTestSuite decodes the first response line as UTF-8 before checking for the opening JSON brace.
Requests now records a response's character encoding from its headers as it builds the response. Request._build_response sets Response.encoding so response content can be handled using that metadata.
Response line iteration now uses a smaller default read size. The ITER_CHUNK_SIZE constant in requests/models.py drops from 10 KiB to 512 bytes.
Requests now accepts a byte-string HTTP method without converting it to a Python bytes representation. Session.request uses to_native_string, and a regression test sends a byte-string GET method.
The GitHub workflows now use version 4.0.0 of actions/checkout. The CodeQL, lint, and test workflows upgrade from version 3.6.0.
Too many redirects can now be suppressed in safe mode. Request.send catches request exceptions while building the response and stores the exception on the response when safe mode is enabled.
This is an empty commit. It contains no file or module changes.

The Unicode multipart field-name test now opens the Python source file for its upload fixture. RequestsTestCase.test_unicode_multipart_post_fieldnames constructs the source filename before reading it in binary mode.

The default user-agent now identifies Requests and its version without including the Python runtime details. The default_user_agent helper is simplified, and .gitignore also adds the PyCharm project directory.
Requests adopts automatic code formatting. The change adds formatting configuration in pyproject.toml and pre-commit and reformats code throughout the requests package.
Request paths now preserve existing percent escapes and allowed punctuation when quoted. Request._build_url and Request._build_response quote paths directly instead of decoding and then quoting them.
This commit tidies the formatting of the response line iterator. Response.iter_lines places both arguments to iter_content on one line.
Requests now percent-encodes redirect destinations supplied in Location headers. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects applies requote_uri to absolute redirect URLs as well.

HTTP Basic header construction avoids a redundant conversion to native text. The _basic_auth_str helper converts the Base64 result before adding the Basic prefix and returns the assembled string directly.
The bundled urllib3 update changes how connection-pool errors are constructed. HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen passes URL, host, and remaining retry information to the relevant exception classes.
The advanced guide adds a section demonstrating common HTTP methods. It introduces the available Requests verb helpers with examples based on the GitHub API.
The project bumps Requests to version 0.7.5. The changelog records that Response.content is None for an invalid response, and requests/__init__.py updates the release identifiers.
Session requests now handle cookie inputs according to their type. Session.request converts dictionaries with cookiejar_from_dict and checks other cookie inputs separately.
Requests adds Python 3.6 to its documented and declared support. The update touches the FAQ, development guide, and setup.py, and adds a Python 3.7 development build to Travis CI.
This commit restores the safe-mode timeout fix. Request.send initializes an empty response path when an exception is suppressed, and the test suite again checks the different timeout outcomes.

The developer guide now gives a complete local setup for running tests with the required dependencies. The instructions in todo.rst use a virtual environment and the Makefile, and the environment directory is ignored.
This commit removes an unused regular expression import from the packaging script. The cleanup drops re from setup.py.
The bundled chardet2 test script now runs under Python 2.7 with print function semantics. The change adds the print_function future import to its test.py.
The project credits Matt Spitz as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst lists the name and GitHub handle under Patches and Suggestions.

Redirect responses can pass the status check in danger mode when redirects are allowed. Response.raise_for_status takes the allow_redirects setting as an argument and uses it to decide whether a 3xx status is an error.
This commit synchronizes the request tests with upstream master. The affected code identified in the change is RequestsTestCase in test_requests.py.
Developers can now validate the README's reStructuredText with a Makefile target. The test-readme target runs the packaging check through Pipenv, and the Pipfile adds readme_renderer.
The invalid timeout test now matches urllib3's updated validation message. TestTimeout.test_invalid_timeout expects the timeout error to list None as an allowed value alongside numbers.
The Requests 3.0 development support heading has updated punctuation. Both documentation sidebar templates add a trailing colon to the heading.
The Requests package version is bumped to 2.17.1. The change updates the version and build constants in requests/__version__.py.

HTTP method names are now normalized during request preparation. PreparedRequest.prepare_method uppercases the method and converts it to a native string, and Session.request drops its earlier conversion.
This commit explains the decoding order for HTTP reason phrases. The comment in Response.raise_for_status describes trying UTF-8 for localized messages before falling back to ISO-8859-1.
Chunked uploads no longer return a connection to the pool twice. HTTPAdapter.send removes the extra manual release on the successful upload path.
The request API docstring shortens its explanation of the data parameter. It retains the list of tuples as a supported form input while removing the separate sentence about repeated field names.

The bundled character encoding detector receives Python compatibility fixes. Requests imports charade through its compatibility module, and the detector corrects byte substitutions and version-dependent type checks.
Requests now exposes RetryError when urllib3 exhausts retries because of a response error. HTTPAdapter.send translates the failure, and a regression test covers urllib3 retry handling.
The cookie documentation now names Python's http.cookiejar module. Docstrings in requests/cookies.py update references in MockRequest, MockResponse, and the cookie jar helpers.

This commit updates the bundled urllib3 connection and response code. The visible HTTPS connection change allows VerifiedHTTPSConnection to skip hostname verification when assert_hostname is explicitly False.
The internationalized URL test now checks the shortened URL differently. RequestsTestSuite.test_idna looks for the shortener hostname, and the test file switches to Python's json module.
The vendored urllib3 package is refreshed with new connection-pool and timeout code. The update exposes Timeout through urllib3 and touches request handling in HTTPConnectionPool.
Requests no longer exposes its old settings object at package level. The package initializer drops the import from requests.config as part of deprecating settings.

The 2.9.0 changelog documents partial file uploads and text-mode upload warnings. HISTORY.rst also records the addition of HTTP status code 511 and explains how upload length accounts for a file's current position.
The Response iterator has a clearer docstring. Response.__iter__ now explicitly says a response can be used as an iterator.
The request API now expands caller-supplied HTTP header values automatically. The request function imports header_expand and applies it to each value in the headers mapping.
The advanced guide now explains how to configure a proxy once for all calls through a session. The documentation adds a Session example alongside the existing per-request proxy instructions.
GET, HEAD, and DELETE now use the same request construction path as other methods. Request.send removes the special case that skipped normal file and body handling for those methods.
The links to earlier security advisories now use the correct MITRE hostname. The vulnerabilities page removes the obsolete www prefix from the affected links.
The README changes how it lays out the list of Requests features. The feature block now uses preformatted markup to preserve the spacing between entries.
The test dependencies now use the final pytest-httpbin 2.1.0 release. Both setup.py and requirements-dev.txt replace the earlier release candidate.

Calls through the functional API now close the temporary session after a request. The request function clears the session's connection pool and sockets to avoid open-socket warnings and apparent memory leaks.
The changelog clarifies which methods respect the option to disable redirects. HISTORY.rst names GET and HEAD explicitly in the corrected entry.

Timeout errors now carry urllib3's original timeout details. Request.send converts urllib3 timeout exceptions to Requests Timeout errors so callers can distinguish socket timeouts from connection-pool timeouts.
This commit prepares the Requests 2.27.1 release. It updates the package version and build number and records the proxy URL parsing fix that keeps the authentication component.
This commit revises how a connection is used during a chunked upload. HTTPAdapter.send reorganizes the low-level connection writes and response handling for streamed request bodies.
OAuth1 now signs requests with body formats outside its usual form handling. The OAuth1 call handler in requests/auth.py can sign the request without including an unsupported body in the signature.
Requests refreshes its bundled CA certificates. The update changes requests/cacert.pem, removes the listed Wells Fargo root certificate, and records the bundle refresh in the release history.
The documentation sidebar now shows $110 raised toward the Requests fundraising goal. Both sidebar templates update the displayed amount from $10.

The test suite adds coverage for preserving URLs that are already percent-escaped. RequestsTestSuite.test_session_with_escaped_url exercises escaped spaces, reserved characters, and non-ASCII characters to catch double encoding.
The project corrects the GitHub link for contributor Jonathan Wong. The update fixes the link markup for the existing AUTHORS.rst entry.
The Requests package version is bumped from 2.4.3 to 2.5.0. The change updates both release identifiers in requests/__init__.py.
The test suite now requires Flask 1.x to keep httpbin working. The constraint in requirements-dev.txt prevents installation of the incompatible Flask 2.0 release.
Requests removes the obsolete requests.monkeys module. The deleted module housed compatibility patches for urllib2's HTTP Basic and Digest authentication handlers.
The tests now check that prepared requests survive a complete pickle round trip. TestRequests compares the restored URL, headers, and body and expands coverage to requests with files and hooks.
The advanced guide shows how to send HTTP methods without a dedicated helper. Its custom verbs section uses the generic request method and gives WebDAV's MKCOL as an example.
The README corrects the spacing in the Requests tagline. The introductory text now has a space between the description of the library and the following sentence.
The bundled urllib3 code now prefers Python's standard MutableMapping implementation. Its _collections module falls back to the vendored implementation if the standard import is unavailable.
The Requests package docstring now capitalizes the library name. The change corrects the heading in requests/__init__.py.

Nonstandard URL schemes such as http+unix now pass through request preparation without HTTP-specific parsing. PreparedRequest.prepare_url limits that handling to HTTP and HTTPS URLs, and tests cover custom schemes.
Requests now supports the MD5-sess variant of HTTP Digest authentication. HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header recognizes the algorithm and uses the digest calculation for that variant.
The project notice now includes the license for idna. The NOTICE file adds the dependency's copyright and redistribution terms.
The escaped URL regression test runs again. RequestsTestSuite re-enables the test that checks already percent-encoded URLs are preserved.
Cookies now persist across requests made through a session. The Session class updates its cookie jar with supplied cookies and saves cookies returned on responses.
This is an empty commit. It contains no file or module changes.
The quickstart now states which media type Requests sets when using the json argument. It explains that the resulting request has an application/json Content-Type header.
Response decoding now falls back to UTF-8 if chardet cannot be imported. Response._detected_encoding returns that default instead of leaving the encoding unavailable.
Requests now tells the server to close the connection on the affected send path. Request.send sets the Connection header to close in requests/models.py.

Copying a prepared request now gives it a separate cookie jar even when the original uses a standard CookieJar. PreparedRequest.copy uses a helper that supports both jar types, and RequestsCookieJar.update copies individual cookies.
The Requests package version is bumped to 2.14.1. The change updates the version and build identifiers in requests/__init__.py.
The quickstart cleans up its example for printing an encoded request URL. The example in quickstart.rst uses standard formatting for the print call.

Requests begins separating request preparation from the older request implementation. The models module introduces PreparedRequest and a shared request mixin, and the Makefile adds a target for exercising the new flow.
The bundled urllib3 dependency is updated to version 1.8.2. The update changes its connection implementation, including how HTTPConnection initializes the source address on older versions of Python.
Users can now choose the retry limit when creating an HTTPAdapter. The adapter constructor accepts a max_retries argument and saves it for subsequent connections.

This commit revises authentication and request hook internals. The auth module removes its built-in HTTPKerberosAuth implementation, and the hooks and models modules are updated around request preparation.
This commit eliminates a duplicate assignment during request initialization. Request.__init__ removes the redundant write to its hooks attribute.
The basic authentication test now exercises non-ASCII credentials. TestRequests runs its credential-tuple test with both plain ASCII strings and UTF-8 encoded Cyrillic credentials.
The test suite backs out the re-enabling of the escaped URL regression test. The change reverts the earlier update to RequestsTestSuite in tests/test_requests.py.

JSON request bodies are now encoded as UTF-8 bytes for upload. PreparedRequest.prepare_body sets the JSON media type with UTF-8 and gives urllib3 a bytes-like body, including for uploads using pyOpenSSL.
The asynchronous request mapper now uses a shared send path for pooled and unpooled jobs. The map function in requests/async.py creates a pool only when a size is supplied.
The development philosophy page now includes an image. The change adds the image near the heading in philosophy.rst.
The documentation now shows the first $10 raised for Requests development. The two sidebar templates update the amount while retaining the $5,000 goal.

The test suite now covers POST requests that follow a 307 redirect with a seekable upload stream. TestRequests adds redirect cases to catch a request getting stuck and updates the test httpbin dependency.

Proxy URLs retain their credentials when Requests normalizes their scheme. The prepend_scheme_if_needed helper restores authentication to the network location, and its tests cover URLs with credentials.
The quickstart explains how the json argument interacts with other request body inputs. It states that Requests ignores json when data or files is supplied.
The cookie tests now check how an expiration value is converted from a morsel. RequestsTestCase exercises morsel_to_cookie to guard against regressions in its expires handling.
Generated coverage and test reports are now excluded from the VS Code file explorer. The change adds workspace file exclusions in .vscode/settings.json.
The project credits Johannes Gorset as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The status check now documents that it can raise a stored URL error. The Response.raise_for_status docstring lists URLError alongside HTTPError.

Cookies sent on the original request are preserved on the response's request record across redirects. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects restores the original Cookie header, and a test covers cookies used through the public API.
The Makefile updates the workflow for refreshing bundled urllib3 and chardet. The new commands clone each dependency before removing and replacing its vendored copy.
The quickstart's status-code example now uses a valid URL string. The requests.get example in quickstart.rst fixes mismatched quotation marks.
The HTTP tests now use httpbin endpoints for several common requests. RequestsTestSuite switches its GET and HTTPS checks to httpbin and checks a custom User-Agent against httpbin's echo.
The documentation sidebar now offers a link for thanking the maintainer. The sidebarintro.html template adds a Say Thanks link to SayThanks.
HTTP-based tests now get their server URLs from a pytest fixture. The tests in test_requests.py accept the injected httpbin fixture for request, authentication, and redirect cases.
Requests now requotes the full URL when building a request, including components outside the path. Request.full_url also begins converting text URL components to UTF-8 as part of assembling the URL.

The public request function now uses the updated hooks interface. It initializes hook and cookie defaults explicitly and dispatches the registered argument, pre-request, and post-request hooks by event.
The API documentation now explains that dictionaries passed as request data are form-encoded. The docstrings for request and the POST, PUT, and PATCH helpers all clarify this behavior.
The Makefile gains a target for installing Requests in editable mode with SOCKS support. The new init target installs the socks extra along with the local package.
The Requests package version is bumped to 2.0.1. The release identifiers change in requests/__init__.py, and HISTORY.rst records the updated CA bundle.
This commit removes the project's standalone NOTICE file. Its deleted content included attribution and license text for vendored libraries such as Poster.
The sponsors page adds a decorative cake and sparkle line. The change appears in the community documentation in sponsors.rst.
The changelog now lists the Requests 0.6.2 release. HISTORY.rst records that the option to disable redirects applies to safe HTTP verbs.
The Requests Pro button now sits in its own paragraph in the documentation sidebar. Both sidebar templates wrap the existing link and button script in paragraph markup.
The package metadata now lives in a dedicated version module. Requests imports the constants from requests/__version__.py, and the packaging script is updated alongside the move.
Project materials now use the correct spacing for the Stack Overflow name. The correction appears in the GitHub issue template and the community support guide.
Request parameter encoding now distinguishes native strings differently on Python 2. Request._encode_params checks keys and values with types.StringType instead of the compatibility alias for str.
Users can now configure proxies when sending a request. The public request API accepts a mapping from protocols to proxy URLs and passes it to the Request model.
The documentation homepage replaces one of its testimonials. The testimonials section in index.rst now features a quote attributed to Matt DeBoard.
The README corrects the displayed label for its documentation link. The link still points to the Requests 2 documentation site.

Test server request handlers can now make received data available to the main test thread. The Server implementation gains this capability, and TestTestServer exercises recovery of two received requests.
A copied cookie jar now keeps its existing cookie acceptance policy. RequestsCookieJar.copy sets the original policy on the new jar so custom policies survive request preparation.

Cookies supplied on an individual request now take precedence over session cookies. Session.request copies the session jar and overlays the request cookies, using the newly implemented RequestsCookieJar.copy.
This commit removes trailing whitespace in the curl command helper. The formatting cleanup is in curl_from_request in requests/utils.py.
The Flake8 task now permits assignment of lambda expressions. The Makefile adds the corresponding E731 rule to the list it ignores.
Request body preparation now recognizes a broader range of string inputs. PreparedRequest.prepare_body checks basestring so those values follow the direct string handling path.
This commit adds comments to help explain how a session request is assembled. Session.request labels the merge of local and session options and the step that attaches context to the response.

Requests JSON decoding errors can now be serialized and restored with pickle. JSONDecodeError.__reduce__ uses the JSON library's implementation to preserve its constructor arguments, preventing failures when errors cross process boundaries.
The tests now import the cookie jar module through Requests' compatibility layer. Test_requests.py uses requests.compat.cookielib in place of the direct standard-library import.
The packaging script stops modifying the bytecode-writing environment setting. Setup.py removes the assignments that set and later deleted PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE.

Requests can now rewind a seekable request body before resending it on a redirect. PreparedRequest stores the original position, and the redirect machinery uses a rewind helper with a dedicated error for a body it cannot rewind.
The project credits Torsten Landschoff as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst lists the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The documentation homepage corrects a spelling error in its description of HTTP/1.1 support. The change is in the introduction in docs/index.rst.
The README updates the stated Requests download count to over 50 million. The change replaces the previous figure of 11 million in the project's popularity statement.
The package description can render correctly on PyPI again. HISTORY.rst marks up the wheel filename pattern as literal text to fix the invalid reStructuredText included in the long description.
The changelog records SSL certificate verification for Requests 0.8.8. The new HISTORY.rst entry describes the verify argument, the bundled certificate list, and an urllib3 update.
The documentation homepage clarifies that urllib3 provides automatic connection pooling and keep-alive. It removes the claim that urllib3 is embedded in Requests.
The quickstart now names Requests as the package readers should have installed. The introduction in quickstart.rst corrects an accidental reference to Tablib.
Users can now stream large response bodies a chunk at a time. Response.iter_content adds incremental reading, with gzip and Unicode decoding helpers in requests/utils.py.
The quickstart clarifies which exception invalid JSON can raise. The Response.json section explains that simplejson can raise its own decoding error on either Python version when installed.
The project copyright year is updated to 2018. The change revises the copyright line in the LICENSE file.
Errors and documentation for invalid URLs now use the standard term scheme. The change updates PreparedRequest.prepare_url and the docstrings for the URL scheme exceptions.
The project credits Lucian Ursu as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The README's main Requests example now uses Python console syntax highlighting. The change updates the language marker on the interactive code block.
The conflicting POST parameters test now runs on pytest 5. TestRequests.test_conflicting_post_params uses pytest.raises as a context manager to check the expected ValueError.

The request model docstrings now distinguish user-created requests from prepared requests. The Request and PreparedRequest classes in requests/models.py receive shorter descriptions with class references.
The HTTPS test URL helper now uses the secure test server address. The httpsbin function in test_requests.py builds its URLs with HTTPSBIN_URL.
The README now demonstrates the correct method for sending a PATCH request. The PATCH example calls requests.patch instead of the POST helper.
The test server tests now have their own test module. TestTestServer moves to tests/test_testserver.py, separating its socket and server lifecycle cases from the utility tests.
The quickstart clarifies that decoding a response as JSON does not indicate HTTP success. The Response.json section covers empty or invalid JSON and explains when to check status separately.
The README fixes the punctuation that introduces its usage example. The change places the reStructuredText literal block marker immediately after the preceding sentence.
The README shortens its statement about supported Python versions. It removes the separate PyPy performance claim while retaining the listed CPython version ranges.
The safe-mode test changes how it checks for a timeout. RequestsTestSuite.test_safe_mode passes requests.get and its arguments directly to assertRaises.
A bodyless GET request no longer gets a default Content-Length header. PreparedRequest.prepare_content_length sets zero length for POST and PUT, and a regression test checks that GET omits it.
The README now lists cookie support as a planned feature. The item is added to the project's roadmap.
Requests now sends only the path portion of the URL to the server as the request target. The Request model separates the full URL used for response metadata from the path used to send the request.
The Requests vulnerability page now names Jeremy Cline as the Red Hat contact. The update replaces Ralph Bean in vulnerabilities.rst and corrects the formatting of an older advisory entry.
The test command now produces colored nose output. The Makefile enables the color option and reqs.txt switches the test dependency to rudolf2.
The quickstart's URL inspection example now uses a print function call. The change updates the example that displays the encoded request URL.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.8.0. The change updates the version and build constants in requests/__init__.py.

The private certificate handling path now requires verification to be enabled. Request.send checks verify before processing the certificate and uses the certificate length to detect the two-part form.
The README's HTTP method examples now show the response returned by the library. The examples replace generic request object placeholders with successful response representations.
OAuth1 now preserves the existing Content-Type header for multipart form data. The OAuth1 call handler removes the redundant header assignment and corrects the related comment.

Sending a prepared request directly through a session now supplies default stream, verification, and proxy settings. The Session.send change is accompanied by updates to the prepared-request and response-hook tests.
The FAQ adds a link to the list of supported Python interpreters. It appears in the response to the Python 3 support question.
Streaming response bodies now handle urllib3's revised exception API. Response.iter_content switches to urllib3 protocol and read-timeout exceptions, and the streaming error tests are updated.
Installing Requests now pulls in chardet as a dependency. The required packages list in setup.py adds chardet version 1.0.0 or newer.
The basic socket server used by the tests is renamed from dummyserver to testserver. The change updates the Server import and renames its test class to TestTestServer.
The project changes how development dependencies are frozen. The direct test requirements are listed without pins in requirements-to-freeze.txt, and requirements.txt records the resolved versions.
The sidebar's fundraising section is now labeled Donate. The change updates the heading in the sidebarintro.html documentation template.
A Response can now be used directly in a with statement. The Response class adds context-manager methods so streamed responses are closed on exit, and the advanced guide and tests show the new usage.
Requests adds a dispatcher for expanding authentication tuples. The dispatch helper in requests/auth.py handles a supplied tuple and leaves an empty authentication value alone.
The packaging metadata now uses a list for its classifiers. The change in setup.py replaces the previous tuple without changing the listed values.
The release history now contains the Requests 2.2.0 changelog. HISTORY.rst records ContentDecodingError and the workaround for proxy bypass failures on Python 2.6 on OS X.
Users can now select a proxy for a particular scheme and host. HTTPAdapter.get_connection checks the host-specific entry before falling back to a scheme-wide proxy.
The public request helper now converts the HTTP method to a built-in string. The request function in requests/api.py normalizes the method before passing it to Session.request.
Requests now uses the URL parser's reconstructed URL to normalize the scheme. HTTPAdapter.get_connection and redirect handling use geturl instead of rebuilding parsed components manually.
Redirect responses no longer carry every cookie saved in the session. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects removes the assignment that replaced response cookies with a copy of the session jar.
Users can now choose raw bytes or decoded text from a response. The Response class returns bytes through content, adds text for Unicode, and makes Unicode decoding opt-in for iter_content.
The advanced guide improves its example of HTTP Link headers for pagination. It shows the returned Link header and introduces Requests' parsed links with a properly formatted example.
This commit reformats the redirect loop for readability. The condition in Request._build_response is wrapped differently in requests/models.py.
The changelog now records the Requests 0.9.2 release. HISTORY.rst lists asynchronous sending, a verification fix, chunked streaming changes, and a fix for response line iteration.
The community guide now recommends Requests-Threads for asynchronous use with Twisted. The guide explains that its session returns awaitable Deferred objects and links to the project.
Requests now installs a default logging handler to avoid warnings when users have not configured logging. The package initializer uses NullHandler or defines a compatible fallback.
The README fixes a missing word in its warning about Python's standard HTTP library. The corrected wording appears in README.rst.
The documentation homepage adds a testimonial from Armin Ronacher. The new entry in index.rst discusses the design of the Requests API.
The response text docstring fixes the spelling of solely. The correction appears in Response.text's explanation of how it determines the encoding.
HTTPAdapter.send again passes the timeout argument directly to urllib3. The adapters module removes the conditional handling that omitted the keyword when the timeout was None.
The Digest authentication streaming test now checks for empty bytes on Python 3. RequestsTestCase.test_DIGEST_STREAM compares raw reads directly with a byte string.
Development tasks now run in a Pipenv-managed environment. The Makefile uses Pipenv for dependency installation, tests, linting, and documentation checks, and the project adds a Pipfile and lockfile.
The session pickling test is enabled again. RequestsTestCase.test_session_pickling restores a serialized Session and checks that it can still send a prepared request.
The Requests 1.0.0 build identifier is corrected. The change updates the build constant in requests/__init__.py while retaining the release version.
Requests now parses proxy and request URLs without lowercasing the whole input first. HTTPAdapter.request_url and select_proxy rely on the URL parser to normalize the scheme and hostname.
Transport adapters are now stored in a defined order for matching URLs. Session uses an OrderedDict for its adapters, and a test covers adapter ordering after mounts are added.
The README rearranges the maintainer and license images below the support statement. The change also adds spacing between the linked graphics.
The documentation's language links now use HTTPS. Both sidebar templates update the URLs for translations including French, German, Japanese, and Chinese.
The cookie parameter test now uses an assertion supported on Python 2.6. RequestsTestCase checks membership using assertTrue in place of assertIn.
The community documentation adds an article about sending JSON with Requests. The link appears in the Articles and Talks section of out-there.rst.
Requests removes its bundled OAuth implementation and dependency code. The change removes requests/_oauth.py and the vendored oauthlib modules and touches the Request model's OAuth-related code.
The sidebar updates the donation service name to Gratipay. The sidebarintro.html template also widens the embedded tip button.
The documentation drops the bundled Sphinx themes maintained by Kenneth Reitz. The removed docs/_themes files included the two theme variants and their supporting templates and styles.
Redirects can now rebuild proxy configuration and proxy authentication for the next request. SessionRedirectMixin adds rebuild_proxies and calls it with the prepared redirect request.
The default test task no longer asks nose for colored output. The Makefile disables the Rudolf color option on the test target.
A request hook can now be registered as a list, tuple, or set of callbacks. Request.register_hook adds the individual hooks to the event, and a regression test exercises registering a list.
The documentation homepage clarifies the list of organizations using Requests. It adds an unnamed federal institution alongside Twitter and fixes the spelling of the Testimonials heading.
Response hooks now run before redirects are followed. Session.send moves the hook dispatch ahead of redirect processing so the hook can see the initial response.
The Flake8 task no longer flags the configured continuation-line indentation rule. The Makefile adds E128 to the ignored checks.
The project stops ignoring the IDE's .idea directory. The change removes that entry from .gitignore.

This commit removes more of the older request configuration interface. It updates the public request API and the Session implementation, including descriptions of the old config and session arguments.
Hook registration now skips non-callable entries in an iterable. Request.register_hook filters the collection before adding callbacks, and a regression test verifies that a string entry is ignored.
Asynchronous requests now always run in safe mode. The wrapper in requests/async.py sets safe_mode in the configuration it forwards to the request call.
The GitHub Actions workflows now use actions/checkout version 7.0.0. The grouped dependency update replaces version 6.0.2 across the affected CI and publishing workflows.
The Requests core module now exposes the HTTPError class it uses. The change imports HTTPError from urllib2 directly into requests/core.py.
Response.content now returns None when the response has no status code. The property checks for an absent or zero status to recognize an invalid response.
A session's custom redirect limit now survives serialization. The Session class adds max_redirects to the attributes saved with the session.
The documentation homepage reports more than 80,000 PyPI installations. The update replaces the previous count of 60,000 in docs/index.rst.
The documentation now includes Sony among the organizations using Requests internally. The addition appears in the adoption list on the homepage.
The package initializer adjusts its imports for Python 2.5 compatibility. Requests/__init__.py drops the absolute-import future directive and uses the older package-local import form.

The expired-certificate test CA is now explicitly marked as a CA. Its OpenSSL configuration adds a critical basic constraints extension so newer OpenSSL releases accept regenerated test CA certificates.
The documentation tree adds a .nojekyll marker. This tells GitHub Pages to serve the generated docs without Jekyll processing.
Requests and responses now support pickling. The Response class defines which state to serialize and restore, and a basic test checks that request and response objects can be pickled.
Requests now accepts chardet version 4. The dependency constraint in setup.py and check_compatibility both allow releases from 3.0.2 up to version 5.
The Requests package is bumped to version 2.18.1. The changelog records a wheel packaging fix, and the version module updates the release identifiers.
The test suite now covers SSL version reporting on Python 2.6. The test in tests/test_help.py checks that requests.help.info works when the OpenSSL version constant is unavailable.
Responses again expose the server's reason phrase. HTTPAdapter.build_response copies the reason from the underlying raw response.
The README validation step now skips Python 2.6 in CI. The Travis build condition avoids invoking the documentation renderer on that unsupported interpreter.
The bundled character detector adds a prober for CP949. The new CP949Prober class lives in the charade cp949prober module.

Upload length calculation now accounts for a file that has already been partly read. The super_len helper in requests/utils.py tracks the current position and uses it to determine the remaining length.
The Requests package metadata now uses the SPDX identifier for its Apache license. The change updates the license value in requests/__version__.py.

The API reference adds more detail about responses, sessions, and exceptions. The updates in docs/api.rst include inherited Response members, the session helper, and common Requests exception classes.
Travis CI returns to running the main Requests test file through the simpleci target. The revert also restores the corresponding Makefile targets and removes the broader non-external test sweep.
The public request helper can now reuse a caller-provided session without forwarding an unsupported keyword. It removes session from the keyword arguments before calling Session.request.
The issue-locking workflow now uses dessant/lock-threads version 6.0.2. The change replaces the version 6.0.0 action reference in lock-issues.yml.
The README restyles its introductory tagline. It uses emphasized text and updates the wording around the heart symbol and the Python community.
The documentation now recommends Pip for installation and pares down the support options. The update also removes the development philosophy and to-do pages and adjusts affected documentation links.
The quickstart clarifies that callers can stream a response to a file without choosing a chunk size. The note in quickstart.rst identifies chunk_size as optional.
The test suite's URL formatting now works on Python 2.6. Tests in test_utils.py use explicit position numbers in their format strings.
The JSON type alias now accepts read-only collection interfaces for its containers. JsonType in requests/_types.py uses abstract sequences and mappings in place of concrete lists and dictionaries.

Header names now go through the same preparation path on Python 2 and Python 3. PreparedRequest.prepare_headers encodes names as ASCII, and the Unicode header-name test runs without a Python 2-only check.
An unreadable .netrc file no longer stops a request. The get_netrc_auth helper catches file access errors and skips .netrc authentication when the file cannot be read.
The documentation adds a countdown to Python 2 retirement. The Sphinx templates display a banner encouraging the transition to Python 3.
The public request functions now declare their return type in their docstrings. The API module gives request and the HTTP verb helpers explicit return fields for requests.Response.
Requests adds PyPy 3.11 support on Linux and macOS and drops PyPy 3.9. The test workflow updates its interpreter matrix, and HISTORY.md records the support change.
The changelog clarifies that integer HTTP header values are no longer accepted. HISTORY.rst notes that some earlier releases allowed them accidentally.
JSON responses now default to UTF-8 when the Content-Type header has no charset. The get_encoding_from_headers helper applies the JSON default to application/json responses.
The quickstart adds a section about OAuth authentication. It points users to the requests-oauth package and links to its documentation and examples.

Imports through requests.packages now preserve the identity of externally installed dependency modules. The packages module aliases loaded urllib3, idna, and chardet modules and their submodules under the old namespace.
The documentation sidebar now includes a Release History link. The sidebarintro.html template points it at the software updates page.
Requests exceptions now use RuntimeError as their base. The RequestException class in requests/exceptions.py changes its inheritance from the general Exception class.
The documentation theme now loads Gumroad's overlay script. The change adds the external script to the Sphinx theme's layout template.
CaseInsensitiveDict is now implemented as a dict subclass. The change in requests/structures.py replaces the older DictMixin base and adjusts its key handling.
This commit removes unused imports from the public API module. The cleanup in requests/api.py drops old model, configuration, status, and hook imports.
Requests now converts a raw socket error to its Timeout exception on the affected send path. Request.send checks the underlying error reason in requests/models.py.

A session now controls whether to read a response body immediately. Session.send forces content loading for non-streaming requests, and HTTPAdapter.send returns the response without doing that itself.
The changelog now mentions Unicode support for URL-encoded data. The change adds that item to HISTORY.rst.
Closing a response works with raw objects that provide no release_conn method. Response.close checks whether the method is present before calling it, and a new test covers the alternative raw object.

The authentication guide now explains where Requests searches for .netrc credentials. It covers the home-directory filenames and NETRC override and shows how to disable the lookup with Session.trust_env.
Travis CI stops running the Requests suite on Python 3.2. The change removes the unsupported interpreter from .travis.yml.
The documentation now includes a development philosophy page in its navigation. The top-level index links to the new docs/dev/philosophy.rst page.
The App Engine adapter now points users to the correct urllib3 documentation. The message in AppEngineManager updates the link to the contrib reference.

The tests add coverage for safe .netrc credential lookup when parsing URLs. TestGetNetrcAuth covers both normal lookups and the security regression, and get_netrc_auth removes an obsolete expanduser workaround.
This commit removes dead commented code for proxy bypass parsing. The cleanup is in HTTPAdapter.get_connection in requests/adapters.py.
The Session initializer now labels the step that processes user-supplied cookies. The change adds an explanatory comment in requests/sessions.py.
The hooks module now describes the request lifecycle events available to callbacks. Its documentation covers the argument hook and the hooks before and after sending a request.
Redirected requests now retain cookies from the session as well as cookies set by the previous response. Session.send passes the session jar to resolve_redirects, which merges both sources.

The advanced guide now links readers to the API references for sessions and configuration. The update replaces a hard-coded list of session attributes and adds a link alongside the configuration example.
The developer guide simplifies installation of the test prerequisites. The instructions in todo.rst use requirements.txt to install them together.
Digest authentication now handles a server challenge with an empty qop field. HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header treats the empty value like an omitted field and produces an authorization header.
The project adds compressed versions of several graphics. The changed assets in ext include the Requests logo and related project images.
The community guide adds a link to rauth for OAuth authentication. The Modules section presents it as an alternative that supports OAuth 1.0 and 2.0.
The authentication guide wraps long lines in its OAuth section. The formatting cleanup in authentication.rst retains the references to requests-oauthlib and its documentation.
The contribution guide now spells out the project's code style. It adds specific guidance about line lengths and quoting strings alongside the existing PEP 8 reference.
The project updates its copyright year to 2013. The LICENSE file also loses trailing whitespace at the end of the text.
The documentation sidebar now shows $253 raised for Requests development. Both sidebar templates replace the previous total of $203.
A closed urllib3 connection pool now raises a Requests ConnectionError. HTTPAdapter.send wraps ClosedPoolError, and a regression test checks what callers receive.
