JSON responses can again be decoded when guessing the UTF codec fails. Response.json catches the Unicode decoding failure and tries the normal Response.text encoding detection path.
The packaging script now identifies the project description as Markdown. Setup.py sets the long description content type to text/markdown for package indexes.
The documentation sidebar gains the Requests turtle logo. The sidebarintro.html template replaces the About Requests heading with a logo linked to the documentation homepage.
The test for .netrc credential handling fixes a spelling error in its comment. TestRequests.test_basicauth_with_netrc_leak now spells credentials correctly.
This commit tidies the style of changes associated with testing timeouts while streaming. The formatting adjustments appear in test_requests.py.
The quickstart corrects a typo in the response status example. The fix appears in the explanation for a successful response and its raise_for_status call.
The Requests package is bumped to version 2.9.0. The release history gives the section its final version and date, and requests/__init__.py updates the build metadata.
The repository removes a machine-specific virtual environment hint. The deleted .workon entry pointed to a local environment directory.

Malformed lists of upload fields now produce a clearer error. Request._encode_files validates the data and file pairs before multipart encoding and reports when an input cannot be converted from two-item tuples.
Request paths with multiple leading slashes are now sent with one leading slash. HTTPAdapter.request_url normalizes the path so urllib3 treats it as a path and a test covers the behavior.
Requests removes the bundled Poster library. The change deletes the package initializer and its multipart encoding and streaming HTTP modules.
The documentation layout is wider so more code fits on screen. The hacks.html template sets a wider content area and adjusts when the sidebar is hidden on narrow displays.
The README presents its feature list in a two-column table. The table groups capabilities such as connection pooling, sessions, and SSL verification into paired entries.
Direct calls to Session.send now honor proxy settings from the environment. Session.send rebuilds default proxy configuration for a prepared request, and tests cover the direct send path.
Request objects no longer use shared dictionaries as the default data and params arguments. Request.__init__ changes both defaults to None.
The 0.13.0 changelog adds cookie and proxy updates. HISTORY.rst records optional cookie persistence, no_proxy support, and RequestsCookieJar improvements alongside the other release notes.
The vendored packages directory now explains where to submit dependency fixes. Its README directs changes for libraries such as urllib3 and charade to their own upstream projects.
The tox suite stops running on unsupported Python 3.3. The change removes py33 from the environment list in tox.ini.
The PUT and PATCH docstrings now describe the optional JSON request body. The change brings those helpers in requests/api.py into line with the POST documentation.
Requests now requires a separately installed certifi package. Setup.py adds certifi version 2017.4.17 or newer to the runtime dependencies.

Prepared requests now use a shared method to calculate the Content-Length header. PreparedRequest.prepare_body and the authentication preparation path use prepare_content_length so the header can be updated consistently.
The changelog adds the Requests 0.3.4 release. The new HISTORY.rst entry records a fix for uploading byte data.
Request and redirect URLs now share the same cleanup logic. The Request model calls get_clean_url in requests/utils.py to centralize URL quoting and assembly.
The authentication guide now shows how to write a custom authentication handler. Its example subclasses AuthBase and implements __call__ to modify and return a request.
This commit corrects indentation in the test socket server. The changes in tests/testserver/server.py cover socket reading and the Server implementation.
The Session class now explains what the trust_env setting controls. Its attribute comment mentions environment-based proxy settings, default authentication, and related configuration.
Requests now rejects unsupported URL schemes during URL preparation. Request.full_url checks the scheme against the HTTP and HTTPS values supplied by supported_schemes, and a test covers the error.
Proxy addresses without a scheme now get one before the connection is opened. HTTPAdapter.get_connection uses prepend_scheme_if_needed with the request URL's scheme.
Cookies saved to the session are now included when preparing the next request in a redirect chain. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects updates the redirected request's cookie jar from the session.
The CA certificate notice no longer includes unnecessary certificate details. The NOTICE cleanup removes the listed issuer, subject, and other metadata from that section.
Tests can now hold the socket server open until the main thread signals it to close. The Server class accepts a close event and lets tests specify how many requests the server should handle.
The documentation restyles its customer testimonials. The homepage changes attribution punctuation, emphasizes the quotes, and links the maintainer handle in one testimonial.

Session calls now have a helper for merging request options with session defaults. The merge_kwargs function in requests/sessions.py combines the dictionaries and removes keys explicitly set to None by the caller.
A response hook can now replace the original response with an HTTP error response. The dispatch_hook helper keeps any returned value other than None, including responses that evaluate to False.
The quickstart now shows how to give one query parameter multiple values without appending brackets to its name. Its example passes a list and shows the same key repeated in the resulting URL.
The quickstart corrects the description of redirect history. It explains that Response.history holds the earlier response objects in order.
Requests adds a module for Python compatibility helpers. The new requests/compat.py centralizes interpreter checks and compatibility aliases.
This commit revises the project's dependency management files. It removes the Pipfile and lockfile and updates requirements.txt.
The Digest authentication calculation now uses the supported auth quality-of-protection value directly. HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header builds that part of the digest only where it is used.

The changelog adds the first set of release notes for Requests 2.3.0. HISTORY.rst documents the default proxy scheme, improved header dictionary display, and authorization and URL handling during redirects.
Reusing Digest authentication no longer makes a normal request body look like a file. HTTPDigestAuth.__call__ clears the remembered file position when the current body is not file-like.
The README moves the Requests logo to a right-aligned image. The change updates the markup for the logo near the project introduction.
The project credits Matt Giuca as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
Digest authentication can now respond to challenges using MD5-sess. HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header recognizes the algorithm and calculates the session form of the digest.

The tests now check that streaming options are honored when Digest authentication resends a request. RequestsTestCase.test_DIGEST_STREAM compares whether the raw response is still readable with streaming enabled or disabled.
The response body is now exposed as an explicit property. Response.content replaces the older dynamic attribute handling, making the attribute discoverable and removing the documentation workaround.
The request argument hook now uses the hooks stored in the session request's assembled arguments. Session.request passes that mapping to dispatch_hook.
The project updates Hugo Osvaldo Barrera's contributor contact details. The change edits the existing Patches and Suggestions entry in AUTHORS.rst.
Redirects that clear the request body now clear attached files as well. Request._build_response passes the adjusted file value when it constructs the follow-up request.
The advanced guide corrects an apostrophe in its description of request configuration. The fix is in the Configuring Requests section of advanced.rst.
The documentation homepage adds package and build badges. The new images in index.rst show information such as the license, wheel availability, supported Python versions, and CI status.
This commit updates the project's test and coverage setup. It adds .coveragerc with vendored packages excluded and revises the Makefile and pytest integration in setup.py.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.8.6. The changelog records socket timeout fixes and proxy authorization support, and the initializer updates the release identifiers.
The quickstart clarifies that a timeout is measured by socket inactivity. The timeout section explains that receiving no bytes for the configured interval raises an exception.
Requests removes its global default for Unicode decoding. The change drops the decode_unicode entry from requests/defaults.py.
Internationalized hostnames now use the installed idna package directly. PreparedRequest._get_idna_encoded_host removes its vendored import and fallback and imports idna normally.
Multipart request data now keeps the correct name for each converted field. Request._encode_files uses the current field name when appending its stringified value.
The proxy bypass decision can now be called independently of environment proxy lookup. Requests extracts the no_proxy checks into should_bypass_proxies and uses that helper from get_environ_proxies.

ASCII-compatible Unicode header names no longer raise a decoding error on Python 2. PreparedRequest.prepare_headers converts those names to native strings, and a regression test sends a request with such a header.

Credentials in a proxy request URL are no longer included in the request line or Host header. HTTPAdapter.request_url uses urldefragauth to remove user information and the fragment before sending the URL to urllib3.
The quickstart now illustrates custom headers with a User-Agent example. The section replaces the JSON POST example with a GET that supplies a headers dictionary.
The CodeQL workflow now uses github/codeql-action version 4.30.8. The change upgrades the initialization, autobuild, and analysis steps from version 3.30.0.
The vendored urllib3 code is refreshed with SSL fixes. The HTTPS connection pool uses helpers for resolving certificate requirements and SSL versions as part of the update.
The Makefile's test target now executes the test script directly with Python. It replaces the parallel nosetests command in the test recipe.
Only known vendored dependencies are now importable through the requests.packages alias. VendorAlias is registered separately for urllib3 and chardet so unrelated names raise an import error.
The cookie request adapter now exposes a host attribute. MockRequest.host returns the same value as get_host for callers that expect the property.
The installation guide restores shell prompts in its command examples. The text shows the prompt for the pip, easy_install, and git clone commands.
The advanced documentation now points to an asyncio option for non-blocking requests. It adds requests-async to the list of related libraries and links to its repository.
Users can now stream response content one line at a time. Response.iter_lines builds on chunk iteration and supports the configured Unicode decoding behavior.

Chunked uploads no longer send a second Host header when the caller already supplied one. HTTPAdapter.send tells the underlying connection to skip the automatic header, and a socket-level test checks the resulting request.
Digest authentication handles redirects more broadly and limits repeated 401 retries. HTTPDigestAuth replaces its specially named redirect hook and updates its retry counter logic.
The documentation removes the banner advertising Requests 3.0 development funding. The cleanup is in the hacks.html template.
The README revises its acknowledgment of the Python Software Foundation. The project attribution now describes Requests as protected by the foundation.

Users can now customize how a session identifies redirect destinations. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects calls the new get_redirect_target method, which a subclass can override to handle malformed redirects.
The README simplifies its early description of Requests. The edit removes the redirect claim from the sentence about ease of use.
Iterating over a failed safe-mode response no longer tries to read a missing raw body. Response.iter_content checks for a raw response, and the test suite adds a case for null responses.
The Requests version is now available as a package attribute. The initializer explicitly imports __version__ from the core module.

The changelog clarifies how early Requests releases handle Unicode and redirects. HISTORY.rst identifies HTTP headers as the basis for decoding and adds notes about header expansion and GET and HEAD redirects.
The project credits David Fischer as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The session documentation now explains what happens when the redirect limit is exceeded. The max_redirects comment in Session states that Requests raises TooManyRedirects.
Requests now allows chardet version 5 as an optional encoding detector. Setup.py and check_compatibility both raise the upper bound to versions below 6.
The requirements now specify a minimum setuptools version. The change adds setuptools 18.5 or newer alongside the existing dependencies in requirements.txt.
The README updates the reference for its GitHub dependent-project count. The popularity paragraph now links the count to the relevant GitHub page.
Prepared requests now retain the caller's custom headers. PreparedRequest.prepare_headers initializes its case-insensitive dictionary from the supplied headers.
The test extra now reuses Requests' SOCKS extra. Pyproject.toml refers to requests[socks] instead of repeating the PySocks version constraint.
The advanced guide clarifies which calls create Request and Response objects. It uses requests.get and related helpers in place of a wildcard method expression.
The sponsors page adds a section for Linode. Sponsors.rst includes a link and a description of the company's cloud hosting service.
The suite drops a test that used httpbin's status-zero endpoint. The removed RequestsTestSuite case had exercised content access on an empty safe-mode response.
GitHub handles in the contributor list now link to profiles. The AUTHORS.rst cleanup also removes handles that do not resolve.
The documentation sidebar now displays a new Requests logo. The change adds the image, links it to the documentation homepage, and adjusts the theme's logo spacing.
CI linting now installs and runs pre-commit directly. The lint workflow pins the tool and checks all files, while Dependabot is configured to skip patch-level action bumps.

HTTPS requests through a proxy no longer receive a proxy authorization header from Requests' redirect handling. SessionRedirectMixin.rebuild_proxies leaves TLS tunnel authentication to the adapter, and regression tests check the header behavior.
The documentation fixes spelling and line wrapping across the user and community guides. The edits include typos in the advanced guide's raw response and parameter descriptions.
Requests now still quotes a URL when the unquoting step encounters an invalid percent escape. The requote_uri helper falls back to quoting the input, and tests cover unquoted percent signs.
The FAQ corrects the grammar in its explanation of an old httplib2 bug. The change is in the comparison with other HTTP libraries.
This commit removes redundant test server files. It drops the old top-level testserver module and an editor swap file under the test server directory.
Basic authentication now uses Latin-1 for encoding credentials. The _basic_auth_str helper switches from UTF-8 and the authentication module drops its unicode_literals import.
The API documentation now gives a logging example that works on both Python 2 and Python 3. The example tries the Python 3 HTTPConnection import and falls back to httplib on Python 2.
The commit message identifies a README update. The indexed text does not describe the exact change.
Requests can now run multiple callbacks for the same hook event. The dispatch_hook helper handles a single callable or a collection and passes the updated result from one callback to the next.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.13.4. The package metadata records the new version and the changelog includes the OAuthlib URL parameter fix.
Cookie conversion now turns Max-Age into a timestamp relative to the current time. The morsel_to_cookie helper in requests/cookies.py also handles a text Expires value separately.

This merge updates contributors, release notes, and response streaming code. The visible changes touch Response.iter_content's chunked generator and note removal of select.poll from Gevent monkeypatching.
The documentation homepage updates its financial support link. The change uses the lowercase form of the maintainer's Cash App address in index.rst.
The documentation now describes the rules for producing Requests releases. The new release-process page is linked from the index and explains how changes affect release version numbers.
The authentication guide now names OpenID Connect alongside OAuth 2. It explains their relationship and directs users to requests-oauthlib for OAuth 1 and OAuth 2 support.
Scheme-specific proxies now take precedence over the all-schemes fallback. The select_proxy helper changes its lookup order, and the tests exercise a configuration containing both kinds of proxies.
Users can iterate over the chunks or lines of a response after its content has already been read. Response.iter_content uses the new iter_slices helper to yield pieces of the cached body.
Requests removes an unused iterator wrapper. The IteratorProxy class and its supporting imports are deleted from requests/structures.py.
The README's example output now matches the current project description. The displayed result is shortened to the description of Requests as a simple and elegant HTTP library.
The test setup now includes the mock package. The change adds mock to reqs.txt.
The vendored urllib3 package is updated to a Python 3-compatible version. The update bumps the bundled version to 1.1 and refreshes its connection pools, responses, and other modules.
The changelog records support for international domain names. HISTORY.rst adds the feature to a provisional Requests 0.5.1 entry.
Basic authentication's credential warning now formats correctly on Python 2.6. The _basic_auth_str helper uses explicit positional indexes in the warning's format strings.
Travis CI now runs the coverage upload command in the Pipenv environment. The after_success step in .travis.yml invokes Codecov through Pipenv.
Requests adds support for signing outgoing requests with OAuth 1. The new OAuth1 authentication class in requests/auth.py uses OAuthLib and exposes options for the signature method and placement.
The documentation homepage improves its explanation of why Requests exists. It revises the comparison with urllib2 and fixes the link to the ISC license.
The publishing workflow now uses version 1.14.0 of the PyPI publishing action. The change updates both pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish references in publish.yml.
The Response.ok documentation now makes clear that redirects can be considered successful. Its docstring explains the below-400 status rule and distinguishes it from testing for HTTP 200.
Requests now prefers the certificate bundle provided by certifi. The where helper in requests/certs.py falls back to the bundled cacert.pem if certifi cannot be imported.
Gzip-encoded HTTP responses are now decompressed automatically. Request._build_response detects the gzip Content-Encoding header and attempts to decode the body with zlib.
The Pipenv development requirements now follow the test versions used in setup.py. The Pipfile also adds Sphinx and Alabaster for building the documentation.
The API documentation now builds without Sphinx treating the keyword-argument asterisks as markup. The docstrings for the public HTTP method helpers escape the asterisks in kwargs.
The project removes its standalone Unicode response test script. The deleted test_unicode.py contained RequestsTestSuite cases for response encodings such as Big5 and ISO-8859-1.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.13.1. HISTORY.rst records file-like request bodies, error responses returned by hooks, and text and JSON fixes for empty responses.
Requests adds a bundled copy of urllib3. The new requests.packages.urllib3 modules provide thread-safe connection pooling and related HTTP helpers.
The development dependency files now use corrected package names. The Pipfile and lockfile update Sphinx and the pytest plugins for mocking and coverage.
The quickstart explains when to use a raw response stream. It describes how Response.iter_content decompresses gzip and deflate data while Response.raw exposes the bytes as received.
The community guide adds a French introduction to Requests. The external article appears in the Articles and Talks section of out-there.rst.
The project credits Rohan Jain as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and handle under Patches and Suggestions.
The documentation theme adds Gauges analytics. Its layout template loads the tracking script asynchronously.
Invalid JSON now returns None if the response cannot be decoded. Response.json catches a failed initial decoding attempt and falls back to the normal text or content path before returning None.
The repository now ignores the generated packaging manifest. The change adds MANIFEST to .gitignore.
The connect timeout test fixes how it checks the exception it receives. TestTimeout.test_connect_timeout removes an empty statement and adjusts the ConnectionError and Timeout assertions.
The documentation homepage removes the decorative symbol from its opening description. The introductory sentence in index.rst starts directly with the library name.
The request URL builder now documents the steps it performs. Comments in Request._build_url explain international domain names, UTF-8 path encoding, quoting, and query parameters.
The newsletter signup is moved lower in the documentation sidebar. Both sidebar templates relocate the Get Updates heading, description, and subscription link.
Response character encoding detection moves into a utility helper. The Response model uses get_unicode_from_response and drops its own lower-level content type and encoding helpers.
The status codes module now imports when Python strips docstrings at optimization level two. The _init function checks for a missing module docstring before trying to update it.
The pre-commit configuration now uses ruff-pre-commit version 0.16.1. The hook revision is updated from version 0.16.0.
Requests now accepts mappings and lists of key-value pairs in more places. The session and utility code share conversion helpers and use OrderedDict where preserving key order matters.
The development setup pins Pipenv to a specific version. The Makefile's init target installs version 3.1.9.
The invalid-port test now fails more quickly when a connection cannot be opened. RequestsTestCase supplies a one-second timeout to its request.
POST and PUT can now send URL query parameters and a request body together. The API passes params and data separately to Request, and tests cover combining the two.
Prepared request paths no longer go through the extra quoting step on Python 2. Request.path_url guards that step by Python version, and a test checks that a path is not escaped twice.
The project updates its pre-commit tool versions. The hook configuration upgrades the pinned tools and the commit applies their resulting source and test cleanups.
The bundled urllib3 dependency is upgraded to the 1.9 series. The vendored update touches its connection pool, HTTP connection classes, and header collection.
The advanced guide fixes its prepared-request example for merging environment settings. The example now supplies an empty proxy dictionary to Session.merge_environment_settings.
The changelog explains the move to callback-based request authentication. HISTORY.rst records the removal of AuthManager and AuthObject and the new tuple-based interface.
The project adds a basic unittest suite for Requests. Test_requests.py defines a RequestsTestCase with setup, teardown, and a simple assertion.
The multipart upload test now also sends an encoded non-ASCII form value alongside a file. RequestsTestCase.test_unicode_multipart_post checks that the server accepts the request.
Users can now supply client certificate and key files for HTTPS requests. The public request helper accepts cert_file and key_file and passes them through Session to the Request model.
The community documentation removes its curated extensions page. The deleted extensions.rst listed third-party additions to Requests.
The PostBin upload tests now use a simpler bin creation request. RequestsTestSuite drops the manual form Content-Type header and restores the assertion that the service responds successfully.
Proxy URLs now require an explicit scheme. HTTPAdapter.get_connection validates them with a utility that raises MissingSchema instead of automatically supplying a scheme.
The documentation homepage repairs the link to an example written without Requests. The change fixes the reStructuredText link markup in the How Simple section.
The README corrects the URL used for its Say Thanks badge. The update escapes the space in the badge text so the image can display.
The development guide updates the supported Python interpreter list. Todo.rst replaces Python 3.1 and 3.2 with Python 3.4 and 3.5 and removes the earlier warning about support.
The advanced guide now explains how to consume a chunked response as it arrives. It recommends streaming the request and using Response.iter_content with no fixed chunk size.
This commit makes a small cleanup around the Request class. The visible change is in requests/models.py.
The project adds the initial skeleton for the Requests package. It introduces the core module, an initializer that exposes it, and a requirements file.
Multipart uploads now skip file entries with a None value instead of raising an error. RequestEncodingMixin._encode_files ignores those entries, and a regression test covers the input.
Requests can now choose whether to preload data for blocking connections. Request.send passes the blocking option to urllib3, and Response.content can read from data that was already loaded.
Authorization is now removed on more redirects that change the URL's origin. SessionRedirectMixin.should_strip_auth preserves the same-host HTTP-to-HTTPS exception only when standard ports are used.
Requests can now send requests to internationalized domain names. Request._build_url encodes the hostname with IDNA before reconstructing the URL, and a test exercises a non-ASCII domain.
The README adds a link for financially supporting the maintainer's open source work. The new note appears near the introductory Requests example.
Digest authentication now uses the public response close method when handling a challenge. HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 calls Response.close instead of releasing the raw connection itself.
CI now tests the final Python 3.10 release and PyPy 3.7. The test workflow replaces the 3.10 development entry and adds an Ubuntu job for PyPy.
Pytest no longer loads its warnings plugin for this project. The change adds pytest.ini and includes it in the source distribution manifest.
Raw socket failures during a request now become Requests ConnectionError exceptions. Request.send wraps socket.error, and tests cover the connection failure with and without safe mode.
Cookie expiration dates are now converted as UTC timestamps. The morsel_to_cookie helper uses calendar.timegm when it parses the Expires attribute.
The release process guide corrects a spelling error in its hotfix rules. The change fixes the word dependencies in the description of vendored library upgrades.
The project trims and reorganizes its introductory documentation. The README and documentation homepage remove a verbose feature paragraph, and the homepage adds a Testimonials heading.
The advanced guide updates its response hook examples to use dictionary literals. The session example now appends the callback to the response hook list.
The project credits Antti Kaihola as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and GitHub handle under Patches and Suggestions.
The README removes its monthly download badge because the displayed data was inaccurate. The change deletes the PyPI download badge near the project heading.
Requests preserves the body of a POST or PUT across the additional body-preserving redirect status. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects expands the set of status codes that keep the prepared body.
The Requests package is bumped to version 2.19.1. HISTORY.rst records an import fix when the status codes module's docstring is missing, and the version module updates the release metadata.
The .netrc helper now exposes an option to raise credential lookup errors. The get_netrc_auth function defaults raise_errors to False, preserving the usual behavior of skipping failed lookups.
The package metadata stops claiming support for Python 3.0. Setup.py comments out the corresponding classifier.
Requests introduces a transport adapter interface. The new adapters module defines BaseAdapter and HTTPAdapter for sending requests, managing connection pools, and cleaning up connections.
The tests now check that a server can expire a cookie stored on a session. RequestsTestCase first saves a cookie and then exercises a response that expires it.
The test dependency entry changes to a minimum version of 2.7. The edit in requirements.txt spells the package name pytestt.
Users can now inspect response headers before downloading the whole body. The Request and Response models defer content reading and expose the underlying response's read and close methods.
The quickstart now explains when Requests changes caller-supplied headers. It documents precedence for authorization, proxy authorization, and content length, including changes during redirects.
Content-Length values for streamed bodies are now prepared as strings. PreparedRequest.prepare_body converts the computed length before setting the header, and the tests cover file-like bodies.

OAuth1 now handles request bodies based on the base media type. The authentication handler normalizes Content-Type, recognizes multipart form data with parameters, and adjusts how it signs requests containing query or body data.
Digest authentication now retries only in response to a 4xx challenge. HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 returns other responses unchanged, and a low-level test verifies the distinction.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.8.9. The package initializer updates the version and build identifiers, and HISTORY.rst records a packaging fix.
Requests now follows redirects whose Location contains only a relative path. Request._build_response constructs a destination using the original URL's scheme and host when needed.
Uploaded file parts now include a filename. Request.send uses the file field name, also routes regular body data through encode_params, and fills in the content type when needed.
Request logging now displays the URL actually being sent, including assembled parameters. Request.send builds the full URL before writing the log entry.
The Travis workflow now runs its CI test target explicitly. It also checks the README on supported Python versions and skips that step on Python 2.6.
Session.request now documents file-like objects as valid body data. The data parameter description adds them alongside dictionaries and bytes.

The advanced guide now provides stable anchors for linking to individual sections. The new labels cover sessions, prepared requests, connection reuse, and streaming and can be used through Intersphinx.
Requests now enforces the redirect limit at the configured boundary. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects rejects a redirect when the count reaches the limit, fixing the extra redirect.
Redirect URLs are now converted to the native string type before sending. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects uses to_native_string when assigning the prepared request's URL.
The bundled urllib3 update restores some PyOpenSSL connections on PyPy. The refresh touches the TLS connection and socket wrapper code and updates urllib3's security warnings.
Requests formally drops support for Python 2.7 and Python 3.6. The change updates CI and release documentation and removes compatibility code for those older interpreters.

Prepared requests now retain the cookie jar used to generate their Cookie header. PreparedRequest stores and copies the jar, and Digest authentication reuses it after extracting cookies from a challenge response.
The CodeQL analysis workflow now uses github/codeql-action version 3.28.5. The change upgrades its initialization, autobuild, and analysis steps from version 3.27.0.
The request suite expands its HTTP and HTTPS coverage for PUT and PATCH. RequestsTestSuite adds separate httpbin cases for the verbs and checks the returned status.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.7.6. The changelog records a Digest authentication fix that includes query data with the request path.
Certificate file paths are now distinguished from certificate and key pairs by type. HTTPAdapter.cert_verify checks whether the certificate argument is a string instead of using its length.
The documentation sidebar adds an option to make a one-time payment. Both sidebar templates link to the maintainer's PayPal page.
The documentation adjusts spacing around the Requests purchase button. The change updates the markup in both sidebar templates.

Chained redirects now use the method and body from the previous hop. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects updates the working request after each redirect, preventing a later hop from reverting to the original POST after a 303.
The packaging script removes an old conditional dependency on simplejson. Setup.py drops the rule that installed it on Python versions older than 2.6.
The contribution guide fixes a spelling error in its description of Requests as feature-complete. The change is in docs/dev/contributing.rst.
Internationalized hostnames now go through UTS 46 processing before IDNA encoding. PreparedRequest.prepare_url enables that mode and adds URL preparation cases for additional Unicode domains.
Flake8 output now goes directly to the terminal. The Makefile removes the redirect to flake8_report.txt from its lint recipe.
The quickstart adds a POST example and shows how to send form data. Its introductory GET example also moves from the GitHub timeline to httpbin.
TimedCache simplifies its implementation of the mapping interface. The changes in requests/structures.py use direct dictionary operations and include the missing key in KeyError.
The project revises how it runs tests locally and on CircleCI. The Makefile calls the setup.py test command and circle.yml configures multiple Python versions with tox and pyenv.
Inactive issues and pull requests are now locked after 90 days. The issue-locking workflow sets the inactivity threshold for both kinds of thread.
Merging cookies now handles the jar update path with a simpler exception flow. The merge_cookies helper drops the inner handler that converted a missing update method to CookieJarError.
Users can now pass JSON data directly to requests.post. The API adds a json argument, and the Session and PreparedRequest paths carry it through to body preparation.
The tests now cover attribute lookup on LookupDict. TestLookupDict checks that existing attributes can be read, missing names are reported, and getattr honors an explicit default.
The project credits Alex as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name and GitHub handle under Patches and Suggestions.
The documentation build upgrades Sphinx to 7.2.6 for compatibility with Read the Docs. The version pin in docs/requirements.txt replaces Sphinx 4.2.0.
The response returned by Session.send now carries the redirect history it collected. The method explicitly assigns that list to Response.history.
The README clarifies the error users may see when cloning Requests. The cloning instructions specify that the suggested Git option addresses an invalid commit timestamp.

The request and response models now use request configuration more consistently. The update in requests/models.py moves away from the old global settings import and touches sending, response construction, and content handling.
The README updates the wording in its Documentation section. The link remains pointed at the Requests documentation site.
The packaging script no longer handles Jython separately when selecting test dependencies. Setup.py removes platform detection and includes pytest-cov in the standard test requirements.
The changelog records changes to the response attributes and calling convention. HISTORY.rst notes that Response.cached was removed, Response.request was added, and arguments are passed by keyword.
Requests stops preloading and caching a default SSL context. The adapters module removes the cached SSLContext setup and changes the TLS connection configuration associated with it.
Certificate verification now uses the verification argument passed to the adapter. HTTPAdapter.cert_verify takes the CA path from verify instead of reading an instance attribute.
The request initializer now recognizes Unicode subclasses when encoding parameters. Request.__init__ uses isinstance for its Unicode key and value checks.
The documentation sidebar updates the name of its Luxembourg sponsor. The sidebarlogo.html template displays CERT Gouvernemental while retaining the GOVCERT.LU link.
This commit backs out the earlier safe-mode timeout change. It restores the old response initialization path in Request.send and removes its corresponding timeout test.
The packaging script now restores the prior bytecode-writing environment setting after installation. Setup.py saves and reapplies the value of PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE.
The project revises its main README documentation. The visible change updates the large text banner in README.rst.
Streaming requests now apply the configured timeout to reads as well as establishing the connection. HTTPAdapter.send sets both limits, and TestTimeout adds a case for a delayed response.

The vendored packages documentation now explains the compatibility stub used by downstream distributions. The README and requests.packages initializer describe how distributions can use external copies of the dependencies.
The package setup adds an OAuthLib dependency. Setup.py lists versions from 0.1.0 up to, but below, 0.2.0.
The documentation homepage expands its example of inspecting a response. The example changes the displayed status and adds an explicit access to Response.content.
Requests replaces its remaining references to charade with chardet. The compatibility import, Response.text documentation, and vendored package guidance use the restored dependency name.
The documentation homepage is brought into line with the README. Its badge section adds a version badge and updates the labels and selection of package information.
The async module now provides a gevent-powered counterpart to the synchronous API. It returns prepared Request objects from the helpers and provides map to send a collection of requests.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.13.9. The initializer updates the release identifiers, and HISTORY.rst records an OAuth fix for POST requests.

This commit cleans up authentication and response handling in the request model. The API drops the old AuthObject import, and Request updates its authentication assignment and the cookie attribute used during response construction.
This commit backs out an unintended change in the Requests tests. The cleanup is near the compatibility imports in tests/test_requests.py.
The Requests package is bumped from version 1.2.3 to 2.0.0. The package initializer updates both the release and build constants.
The request API now offers a return_response option to control whether a request is sent immediately. The async wrapper disables that option so it receives an unsent Request to dispatch later.
POST redirects now follow the browser-style method change without checking strict_mode. Request._build_response applies the GET rewrite on the affected redirect status codes directly.
The documentation theme hides an inline Revsys element. The Flasky stylesheet adds a display rule for that element.
Converting a cookie morsel no longer raises a TypeError for unexpected keyword arguments. The morsel_to_cookie helper stops passing flags that create_cookie does not accept.
The repository now ignores two local Python test scripts. The .gitignore change adds t.py and t2.py.
The contributor list updates Kenneth Reitz's GitHub handle and profile link. The change is in the existing entry in AUTHORS.rst.
The test requirements now include nose. The change adds the runner to reqs.txt.
The packaging script adds a reference for readers who want to learn more about its setup conventions. The change is a comment in setup.py.
The documentation sidebar now points its donation links and widget to Gratipay. Both sidebar templates update the service address and make the embedded button wider.
The documentation sidebar adds a link to the Open DSM-5 project. The change adds an entry to sidebarlogo.html's link list.
Sessions can now prepare requests with a standard CookieJar without crashing. Session.request copies the jar with the standard copy helper and adds request cookies individually.
The advanced guide's cookie example now displays decoded response text. The example in advanced.rst reads Response.text instead of Response.content.
The quickstart clarifies the introduction to its OAuth examples. The edit completes the sentence about different forms of OAuth and formats the example marker.
The test suite adds coverage for saving and rewinding a request body's position. TestRequests checks non-streaming bodies, successful rewinds, and the error when a stream cannot seek.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.10.2. HISTORY.rst records URL and decoding changes and an attempted fix for running out of open file descriptors.
URL preparation now always requotes the assembled request URL. PreparedRequest.prepare_url simplifies the encoding path and removes the old commented configuration logic.
Printing or logging a CaseInsensitiveDict now shows a regular dictionary of its entries. The new __str__ method in requests/structures.py provides that representation for headers and other uses.
The project credits Chris Dary as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
Cookie policy checks on Python 3.3 can now read the request's unverifiable attribute. MockRequest supplies that attribute through its existing is_unverifiable method.
Requests adds safe_mode to its default configuration. The setting in requests/defaults.py is disabled by default.
The Pipenv lockfile refreshes the development dependency set and package source metadata. The recorded versions now include packaging, pyparsing, and appdirs.
A proxy URL without a hostname now fails before Requests tries to create a proxy connection. HTTPAdapter.get_connection raises InvalidProxyURL, and a regression test checks the invalid URL.
The changelog now records support for sending file uploads and regular POST data in the same request. The note is added to HISTORY.rst.
The changelog corrects the release date for Requests 0.8.0. Its HISTORY.rst entry also notes that uploads send real filenames.
The package metadata now declares the ISC license. Setup.py changes the license classifier from MIT to ISC.
The documentation homepage adopts the Requests tagline HTTP for Humans. Its introductory text also describes the project as an ISC-licensed Python HTTP library.
The HTTP verb helpers now use arguments consistent with the generic request function. Requests/api.py updates their signatures, including optional headers, parameters, and timeouts.
The changelog adds a provisional Requests 0.6.5 entry. HISTORY.rst records the addition of a fast offline test suite.
The Travis test matrix now includes PyPy 3. The change also adds socket cleanup in the test server used by the suite.
The changelog records changes for Requests 0.10.0. HISTORY.rst mentions the ISO-8859-1 text default, support for multiple hooks, and Response.register_hook.
The repository removes a local shell environment file. The deleted .env activated a specific development virtual environment.
This is an empty commit. It contains no file or module changes.
The advanced guide now links directly to the Mozilla trust store. The reference appears in the description of the project CA certificate bundle.

A 307 redirect now preserves the original request body and its content length. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects clears them only for other redirect statuses and handles the Cookie header separately.

The PreparedRequest documentation now advises users how to obtain an instance. The class docstring says to prepare a Request and warns that constructing a PreparedRequest manually can have undesirable effects.
Digest authentication now handles text before hashing it. The MD5 and SHA-1 helpers inside HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 encode string inputs as UTF-8.
Project references now point to the updated Requests GitHub repository path. The changes span the README, release history, documentation, and repository links in comments.
Digest authentication challenge parsing now works with Python 2.6's regular expression API. HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 compiles the case-insensitive pattern before removing the digest prefix.
Redirected requests no longer reapply the original request's query parameters separately. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects removes the params argument when constructing the follow-up request.
Read the Docs now has a dedicated requirements file. The file pins Sphinx to 4.2.0 to keep the documentation build predictable.
The project credits Dj Gilcrease as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The documentation homepage clarifies the attribution of its government users. It describes the cited federal institutions as preferring to remain unnamed.
The changelog adds a section for the next Requests release. HISTORY.rst creates a development entry with headings for improvements and bug fixes.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.13.8. The package initializer updates the release identifiers, and the changelog records HTTP Link header support.
The Response.raise_for_status docstring now describes the HTTPError it raises without calling it a stored exception. The edit reflects that the method creates the error when it is called.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.2.1. The changelog records multipart file uploads for POST and PUT and a Request.url attribute used for context and redirects.
The version module now also carries general package metadata. Requests/__version__.py adds the project description, website, and author contact field.
The install requirements now choose the character detector based on the Python version. Setup.py uses chardet2 on Python 3 and chardet on older Python while keeping certifi.
Multipart uploads now preserve headers set by Poster when applying caller headers. Request.send updates the existing header mapping instead of replacing it.
The documentation now specifies the order of redirect history. The quickstart and Response model describe entries as ordered from the oldest to the most recent.
The HTTPAdapter documentation no longer describes max_retries as restricted to integers. The change removes the integer type marker from the parameter's docstring.
The redirect cookie test now checks the correct response. RequestsTestSuite.test_cookies_on_redirects reads the third response when verifying that the preview cookie was not sent.
The default headers now advertise compression formats through Accept-Encoding. The configuration in requests/_config.py also begins defining default lists for request hooks.
The API migration guide now links to a detailed write-up about Requests 2.0. The added reference in docs/api.rst points readers to Cory's article for API and bug-fix details.
The changelog corrects which OAuth version is supported experimentally. HISTORY.rst changes the release note from OAuth 2 to OAuth 1.
The request preparation code adds a check for generator bodies. PreparedRequest.prepare_body is intended to reject them explicitly with a NotImplementedError.
Requests adds a separate test module for external service checks. The new test_requests_ext.py covers cases including SSL hostname verification and session behavior.
The JSON response docstring receives a whitespace cleanup. Response.json still describes that parsed responses can yield dictionaries, lists, and other values.
The documentation configuration updates the copyright year and tidies its formatting. The changes are in docs/conf.py.
Session option merging avoids retrieving the dictionary keys on every iteration. The merge_kwargs helper stores the keys once and reuses them for matching.
The advanced guide now explains that a hook callback must handle its own exceptions. Unhandled exceptions propagate to the code calling Requests, so callers should handle them as needed.
Session hooks are again merged using the shared settings behavior. The merge_hooks helper delegates to merge_setting instead of constructing unions of callbacks.
This commit reverts an earlier documentation update. It rolls back changes to the sidebar templates and homepage and removes the associated native.js script.
Callers can now request errors from a failed .netrc lookup. The get_netrc_auth helper adds ignore_errors, which defaults to suppressing parse and permission failures.
Requests no longer advertises the compress encoding by default. The default_headers helper keeps gzip and deflate in Accept-Encoding.
Preparing a request body now handles streams that report an unsupported operation. PreparedRequest.prepare_body catches io.UnsupportedOperation alongside its existing exceptions in that path.
Custom transport adapters can again supply their own SSLContext for HTTPS connections. HTTPAdapter exposes build_connection_pool_key_attributes so subclasses can override the urllib3 pool settings.

The project fixes spelling and wording across its documentation and source comments. The corrections include the Sphinx theme README and descriptions of session cookies, redirects, and request handling.
The API reference fixes incorrect numbers in its status-code lookup examples. The updated examples in docs/api.rst show the intended status values.
The advanced guide explains why total connection time can exceed the configured connect timeout. It notes that urllib3 applies the timeout separately when trying each IP address for a hostname.

The early Requests API now reads supplied cookies from the cookies keyword. The public helpers in requests/core.py forward that value to the Request model, which also simplifies checks for an existing cookie jar.
Python 3 callers can now prepare a request with a bytes URL. PreparedRequest.prepare_url decodes the input as UTF-8 instead of including Python's bytes representation, and a test exercises that path.
Coverage measurement now excludes vendored dependencies. The .coveragerc file omits modules under requests/packages.

The Requests package is bumped to version 0.14.0. The changelog records that iter_content can be used after the body has already been downloaded, and the package initializer updates the release metadata.

The security disclosure instructions now direct users to open a private draft security advisory on GitHub. The community vulnerability page points to the project's security policy and updates its Red Hat contact information.

Request sending now builds the body and headers before creating the underlying urllib2 request. Request.send in requests/models.py shares the final dispatch path for form data and multipart file uploads.
The old request helper's documentation drops the description of return_response. The change removes that parameter from the old_request docstring in backup.py.
The test suite now waits one second during server setup. RequestsTestSuite.setUp changes the previous brief sleep to allow more startup time.
Certifi becomes optional for Requests installations. The advanced guide explains that Requests can use certifi when present and otherwise uses its bundled CA certificates.
HEAD requests now leave redirect following disabled by default. The head helper sets allow_redirects to False unless the caller provides a value.

Authentication now has a dedicated page in the user guide. The new authentication.rst collects the available authentication methods, is linked from the documentation index, and replaces the longer quickstart coverage.
The tox matrix drops Python 2.4. The change removes py24 from the interpreter list in tox.ini.
The .netrc lookup stops searching after finding the first available file. The get_netrc_auth helper also simplifies the return path when no file is found.
Cookie tests now use assertions available on Python 2.6. The test_cookies.py changes replace newer unittest methods with equivalent boolean assertions.
The quickstart now distinguishes binary and decoded response data. Its response examples show Response.text for Unicode and explain the role of Response.content when callers need bytes.
This merge brings incremental response body reading into Requests. Response.iter_content can stream chunks, with utility helpers for Unicode and gzip decoding.
The header validation test now actually verifies that accepted header values were kept. TestRequests.test_header_validation turns the comparison into an assertion.
Response text decoding now uses HTTP header information instead of scanning HTML metadata. The get_unicode_from_response helper removes content-based charset detection and an incidental debug print.
Existing callers can again use get_environ_proxies with only a URL. The helper makes its new no_proxy argument optional to preserve the previous calling convention.
Requests restores form-encoded request bodies on the affected upload path. Request.send uses the encoded data and sets the form media type when ordinary request data is present.
The keep-alive tests now use range for iteration. KeepAliveTests.make_requests replaces xrange so its loop works on Python 3.
The FAQ adds a statement about Python 2.7 support. It describes the project's then-current plan to retain support until pip drops Python 2.7 and recommends Python 3.

GET and HEAD calls now honor an explicit request to disable redirects. The API helpers supply a default, and the Request redirect logic uses the option instead of following merely because of the HTTP method.
This commit moves basic GET requests onto the urllib3 transport. The Request model begins using urllib3 and reads the new response status and header interface.
The documentation sidebar now identifies the Requests sea turtle by name. Both sidebar templates update the logo image's title to Rezzy the Request Sea Turtle.
The Requests configuration module moves to a private name. The commit renames requests/config.py to requests/_config.py.
Digest authentication initializes its hash function variable before checking the available algorithms. HTTPDigestAuth.build_digest_header avoids a NameError when no algorithm selects a function.
The documentation homepage fixes a broken link to the Requests 3.0 support page. The change corrects the reStructuredText markup in the funding paragraph.
The prepared-request example now renders as a code block. The advanced guide fixes the markup that introduces its environment settings example.
Session.request regains its public documentation. The restored docstring explains that the method prepares and sends a request, returns a Response, and accepts URL and body options.

Windows proxy bypass checks now handle both registry value types for ProxyEnable. The proxy_bypass_registry helper converts the setting to an integer, and tests cover both representations with ProxyOverride.
The packaging script drops the vendored OAuth libraries from its package list. Setup.py retains a version-specific branch based on the Python 3 compatibility flag.
Session.send now accepts a prepared request created by another copy of Requests. It rejects unprepared Request objects explicitly, and a test checks that they still produce a clear error.
The documentation's logo sidebar removes its Translations section. The change deletes the language links from sidebarlogo.html.
Requests now refreshes its vendored libraries from tagged releases. The Makefile checks out the latest tags for urllib3 and chardet before copying the package files.
The tox configuration stops installing Requests and its SOCKS dependencies a second time. Tox already installs the project, and the test dependencies already include PySocks.

Certificate handling now distinguishes HTTPS from HTTP before applying verification settings. HTTPAdapter.cert_verify branches on the URL scheme first, and a test covers an HTTP request with a certificate argument.
Requests now measures seekable in-memory bodies without copying their contents. The super_len helper seeks to the end to find the size and restores the previous position for partially read bodies.
The commit message identifies a README update. The indexed text does not describe the exact change.
The sponsors page renames its Corporate Sponsors section to Community Sponsors. The change updates the heading in sponsors.rst.
Requests now distinguishes URLs with a missing scheme from URLs with a missing host. PreparedRequest.prepare_url checks them separately and raises InvalidURL for the missing network location.
The cookie utility code now gets SimpleCookie from the Requests compatibility layer. The import in requests/utils.py replaces the direct Python 3 standard-library import.
The status-code module revises the check for aliases starting with a slash or backslash. The loop in requests/status_codes.py combines both prefix tests into a single startswith call.
The README's early response example now shows a content attribute. The change adds the body field to its sample response representation.
POST redirects with status 303 now use value comparison to detect the status. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects uses equality so the existing method rewrite reliably runs.
Project links now favor HTTPS. The change updates URLs in the release history, license, documentation, CI files, and source comments.
The advanced guide repairs a link in the transport adapter section. The updated reference points to the dated location of the essay about Python HTTP.

Basic authentication now converts text credentials to bytes before Base64 encoding and converts the result back to text. Requests/auth.py also stops coercing credentials when HTTPBasicAuth is initialized.
The CodeQL workflow now uses github/codeql-action version 3.23.0. The change updates the initialization, autobuild, and analysis steps from version 3.22.11.
This commit simplifies the fallback path for response text decoding. Response.text checks for empty content before entering the block that handles decoding errors.
Response text can now be read even if no encoding is available. Response.text catches the TypeError from a missing encoding and retries conversion with replacement for invalid data.
Sessions no longer list timeout among the attributes to serialize. The Session class removes the obsolete entry because timeout is no longer a session-level setting.
Requests can now upload files alongside ordinary form fields. Request.send combines the files and form data for multipart encoding, while the initializer retains both the original and encoded data.
Compatibility checks now use at most three components of the urllib3 version string. The check_compatibility function ignores additional components after major, minor, and patch.
Requests now accepts chardet 7 as an optional dependency. The chardet extra in pyproject.toml and the runtime compatibility check both increase the upper bound to versions below 8.
This commit removes trailing whitespace from documentation files. The cleanup covers the quickstart, documentation manifest, and files in the Sphinx themes.
The GitHub workflows now use actions/checkout version 5.0.0. The change upgrades the checkout step in the CodeQL, lint, publish, and test workflows.

Prepared requests now pass the JSON argument through to body preparation. The changes in requests/models.py update the body-selection condition, and the test checks the outgoing request's Content-Type header.
The CodeQL workflow now targets the main branch. The push and pull request triggers in codeql-analysis.yml both switch from master to main.
The compatibility module now exposes quote_plus and unquote_plus on both Python versions. The utilities module imports the new quoting helpers through requests.compat.
Response URLs now use Unicode strings. Request._build_response decodes its full URL as UTF-8, and the new regression test checks the type of Response.url.
The project credits Matt Kohl as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and GitHub profile to Patches and Suggestions.
The settings object now supports a verbose output option. The Settings class in requests/config.py adds verbose to its recognized attributes.
The quickstart now uses the right keyword when setting a cookie's domain. The RequestsCookieJar example changes site to domain for both cookies.
The default Makefile test target now runs pytest without parallel or boxed execution. The tests directory stays the target of the command.
The advanced guide adds an explanation of Server Name Indication for HTTPS. It describes virtual hosting and lists how Python 2 users can enable SNI support with extra dependencies.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.7.0. The change updates the changelog heading and the version and build identifiers in requests/__init__.py.
The contributor list removes its separate urllib3 subsection. The AUTHORS.rst change drops the heading and the entry shown beneath it.
On Python 3, Requests now imports the bundled chardet package directly. The compatibility module removes the old import that aliased chardet2 to chardet.
Socket test servers now shut down when a test fails or opens no connections. The Server context manager interrupts the blocking accept operation before joining, and tests cover both shutdown cases.
Requests now encodes incoming form values as UTF-8 before URL encoding. The Request initializer in requests/core.py also makes the URL builder's data argument optional.
The advanced guide capitalizes Session when referring to the class. The edit fixes two occurrences in the session examples and explanation.
The cookie request adapter now has the type attribute expected by Python 3.3. MockRequest saves the URL scheme as its type and returns it through get_type.
The test suite adds a failing case for form fields set to None. RequestsTestSuite asserts that POST keeps a normal field and omits the field with no value.
The project copyright year is updated to 2016. The change revises the notice at the top of the LICENSE file.
The documentation enables source links and hides the Sphinx footer attribution. The changes update docs/conf.py and also fix a spelling error on the documentation homepage.
The basic test server test now sends and expects bytes over its socket. TestDummyServer.test_basic uses byte strings for both the question and answer.
The documentation homepage now reports more than 16 million downloads from PyPI. The update replaces the 12-million figure in index.rst.
The bundled urllib3 collections can now import on platforms without threading support. The _collections module provides a no-op RLock context manager when threading.RLock is unavailable.
Requests can now bypass a configured proxy for destinations on an exclusion list. Request.send splits and trims the no-proxy entries and checks for a match against the request host.
The test suite removes a broken representation test for CaseInsensitiveDict. The change deletes test_repr from TestCaseInsensitiveDict in test_requests.py.

This commit revises the early request and session implementation. The Request model changes its transport imports and HTTP error handling, and the test changes include cookie and response status cases.
The changelog starts planning the Requests 0.7.1 release. HISTORY.rst lists a move away from urllib2 authentication and the removal of AuthManager.
The README updates its description of the HTTP implementation underlying Requests. The introductory overview names httplib in place of urllib2.
The documentation logo sidebar removes a horizontal rule. The change simplifies the markup in sidebarlogo.html.
The redirect tests now expect an empty proxy mapping by default. TestRedirects updates the expected proxies keyword to match the current request settings.
The duplicate cookie-name test now checks that both cookies were actually stored. TestRequests verifies that two entries with different domains remain in the jar.
The documentation sidebar removes the direct Bitcoin donation line. The change deletes that payment text and link from sidebarlogo.html.
This commit reverts an earlier change to response handling in the Request model. Request._build_response removes the added calls that consumed response bodies to release sockets.
The project credits Kevin Burke as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The invalid header error now formats the name and value together. The check_header_validity helper still describes the required string or bytes types and reports the actual type.
The documentation corrects the title text for its sea turtle logo. Both sidebar templates use the library name Requests in the image title.
The documentation's GitHub buttons now refer to the repository under its new owner. Both sidebar templates change the owner value in the embedded watch button.

Requests now supports choosing a .netrc file through the NETRC environment variable. The get_netrc_auth helper uses the specified path when present, and the quickstart documents the usual search locations.
Travis CI now sends coverage results to Codecov after a successful build. The .travis.yml change adds a post-success upload step.
The release process link in the changelog now uses reStructuredText syntax. The fix in HISTORY.rst lets the link render in the generated documentation.
The documentation index simplifies the navigation under its community section. It removes a separate nested table of contents around the FAQ entry.
The Request initializer stops automatically converting params to a dictionary at this point in preparation. The change removes that assignment from requests/models.py.
The project moves its settings code out of the core module. The API and package initializer change how they reference the context-managed settings object.
The Travis configuration corrects the name of the test server environment variable. It spells the setting HTTPBIN_URL so the tests can read it.
This commit removes an unused cookie class import from the request models. The cleanup drops SimpleCookie from requests/models.py.
The request helper now picks up its default timeout from the shared settings object. The changes in requests/api.py and requests/config.py also revise how the helper reads optional arguments.
Reading response text now falls back when the declared character encoding is unknown. Response.text catches LookupError and retries conversion without the specified encoding.
The packaging script fixes the expression used to read its license text. Setup.py completes the call that reads the LICENSE file.
This commit adjusts whitespace in the request models. The formatting change is in the utility imports in requests/models.py.
Installing from requirements.txt now also installs the local Requests project in editable mode. The change adds the current directory to the requirements file as an editable entry.
The packaging script now supports installing Requests in development mode. Setup.py prefers setuptools and falls back to distutils when setuptools is unavailable.
The support page now publishes the PGP fingerprint for Lukasa. The change fills in the maintainer's entry in the list of security contact keys.
This commit simplifies the older request and authentication models. It removes commented-out AuthObject setup from Request initialization and touches the associated response-handling code.
Invalid URL errors now work correctly on Python 3. PreparedRequest.prepare_url passes the original exception arguments to InvalidURL instead of trying to read a missing message attribute.
This commit prepares the Requests 2.20.0 release. HISTORY.md records removal of authorization on HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects and proxy bypass support for URLs without hostnames.
The bundled urllib3 now verifies the certificate hostname when given CA certificates. VerifiedHTTPSConnection uses a bundled hostname matching helper and reports a mismatch as an SSL error.
The test suite now uses omnijson for JSON handling. Test_requests.py imports the wrapper and tox installs it as a test dependency.
This commit fixes spacing in the contributor list. The edit adjusts the Aram Dulyan entry in AUTHORS.
The session cleanup test now asserts the correct state of an unread response. TestRequests verifies that the response content has not been consumed.
The quickstart makes its HTTP method examples more consistent. The POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS examples use the same quoting style.
The Session API docs now list file-like objects as an accepted request body. The POST, PUT, and PATCH docstrings update their descriptions of the data argument.
The request documentation now lists a sequence of key-value tuples as valid URL parameters. The request and get docstrings and Request model update the description of params.

The OAuth fallback no longer inserts the vendored packages directory into Python's global search path. Requests/_oauth.py aliases the bundled oauthlib module directly, avoiding interference with chardet imports on Python 3.
The sponsors guide now thanks people who support Requests individually. It adds an Individual Sponsors section recognizing both financial and code contributions.
The documentation homepage expands its example of reading a GitHub response. It now uses the user endpoint and shows the status, media type, character encoding, response content, and parsed JSON.
Repeated proxy bypass checks can now reuse cached results instead of repeating slow hostname lookups. The utilities use TimedCache, which expires old entries and evicts the oldest entry when full.
The source distribution no longer includes requirements.txt explicitly. The change removes it from the file list in MANIFEST.in.
The test suite drops a case for sending a generator as a chunked upload. The removed test_chunked_upload method was part of TestRequests.
The development setup now installs test dependencies from requirements.txt. The same commit updates HISTORY.rst to describe Response.json as a callable method.
The project updates the Requests logo image. The changed graphic is ext/requests-logo.png.
The transport adapter preserves the underlying exception on the affected request send path. HTTPAdapter.send re-raises the original error instead of replacing it with a generic Timeout message.
The repository stops ignoring the IDE's .idea directory. The change removes that entry from .gitignore.
The invalid header error message now separates its words correctly. The _validate_header_part helper adds the missing space before the rest of the message.
Requests now has a setting to advertise gzip support by default. The configuration adds accept_gzip, and the Request model adjusts how it applies base and caller-provided headers.
This commit removes leftover commented-out debugging code from redirect handling. The cleanup is in HTTPRedirectHandler.http_error_301 in requests/monkeys.py.
SOCKS proxy handling now imports its manager from the installed urllib3 package. The adapters module also updates its return type references to urllib3's public namespace.
The release process guide adds an introductory image. The change inserts it below the heading in release-process.rst.
This commit reverts unintended edits in the utility tests. The small cleanup is in tests/test_utils.py around the compatibility imports and content-encoding tests.
Retry configuration works with unvendored urllib3 again. The adapters module imports Retry directly from the urllib3 retry submodule through the compatibility namespace.
The project adds the ISC license text. The LICENSE file records the copyright and the terms for using and distributing Requests.
The FAQ adds an image below its main heading. The change is in docs/community/faq.rst.
More HTTP methods are now converted to GET on the affected redirects. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects extends the rule from POST to methods other than GET and HEAD.
The test suite now covers adapter mount prefixes with and without a trailing slash. TestRequests checks how Session.get_adapter matches those prefixes against request URLs.
The README adds another spacer below its attribution paragraph. The change inserts a second empty HTML paragraph.
The project credits Justin Murphy as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The README removes an unnecessary comma from its installation section. The edit corrects the closing satisfaction line in README.rst.

The prefetch tests now check directly whether the response body was consumed. RequestsTestSuite replaces assumptions about iter_content failing with assertions that the body remains unread after a redirect or delayed send.
Users can now read the server's HTTP reason phrase through Response.reason. The new property forwards to the raw response.
Redirect handling now uses the named constants from the status code registry. Request._build_response also checks the configured maximum redirect count in place of a fixed limit.
The test workflow updates its Python setup action from version 2.3.4 to 4.7.0. The change is in run-tests.yml.
The README adds a badge listing the supported Python versions. The badge appears near the project heading and links to the Requests package on PyPI.
The request's sent flag is now set after sending. Request.send records that state in requests/models.py.
This commit removes the old requests/patches.py file. The deleted module contained a header identifying it as request monkey-patch code.
The Digest authentication implementation gives its hash helpers clearer names. HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 labels the UTF-8 MD5 and SHA-1 functions and uses a named variable for the selected algorithm.
The bundled urllib3 SSL base error now derives from Exception. The change updates BaseSSLError in its connectionpool module.
A session with a redirect cache can now be pickled. Session serializes the RecentlyUsedContainer as a dictionary and reconstructs the cache when the session is restored.

Proxy authentication now supports a username with an empty password. HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers generates the authorization header when the username is present, and tests cover both empty and populated passwords.
The README's authentication example now shows the types of returned values more clearly. It updates the status display and shows the content type and body as strings.
The changelog adds Eventlet and Gevent monkey-patching support. HISTORY.rst also updates the existing note about cookie support.
A session can now return an unsent request. Session.request adds the return_response option and returns the Request object when that option is disabled.
The test socket server moves into the tests directory. Its Server implementation and package initializer now live under tests/testserver.
Requests introduces a Session object for sharing settings across calls. The new requests.session module maps the public request helpers and persists cookies, authentication, and proxies.
The advanced guide fixes incomplete httpbin hostnames in its hook examples. The example requests now use the httpbin.org domain.
The Requests package is bumped to version 2.6.2. The changelog records a regression fix for compressed responses sent with chunked transfer encoding.

Content-Type parameter parsing is simplified and now has more coverage for quoted values. The _parse_content_type_header helper centralizes the characters it strips, and the test includes double quotes.
Request construction no longer enables the redirect chain flag by default. The change sets Request.__init__'s redirect argument to False when omitted.
The header validation tests now verify that an error names the offending header. TestRequests captures InvalidHeader and checks the message for each invalid header value tested.
The test suite now runs with pytest 8. The development requirements allow versions below 9, and the HTTPS warnings test stops using the removed None argument.
The Requests package is bumped from version 0.6.1 to 0.6.3. The change updates the version and build identifiers in requests/core.py.
The project removes older development and configuration files. The cleanup drops the HACKING guide, the Settings module, and tox.ini.

Request parameters now encode string values correctly when supplied through iterable types other than lists. Request._encode_params handles general iterables while treating a string as one value, and a new test exercises that case.
The documentation homepage now lists Work for Pie as an organization using Requests. The addition includes a link in the adoption list.
The Windows CI build now upgrades pip through the Python interpreter. The AppVeyor install step uses the module invocation to avoid replacing a running executable and also upgrades wheel.
The test suite now runs in parallel through pytest-xdist. The Makefile launches nine boxed workers, and the development and setup test requirements add the plugin.
The vendored urllib3 package is bumped from 1.13.1 to 1.14. The refresh touches connection pool handling and updates how its logger formats messages.
Requests adds a custom redirect handler and support for recording redirect history. The Request and Response models integrate HTTPRedirectHandler and expose the history of prior responses.
This commit corrects spacing in the HTTP Link header parser. The parse_header_links helper reformats the arguments to the regular expression split call.
The packaging script now extracts the version with a single search. Setup.py reads requests/__init__.py and matches the version assignment without looping over lines.
The request sending code removes an assignment that marked the operation unsuccessful. The change is confined to Request.send in requests/models.py.

The Requests 2.5.1 release notes now describe its behavior changes and fixes. HISTORY.rst covers status errors, URL parsing, non-string upload filenames, and renegotiating Digest authentication nonces.
