Prepared requests can now send themselves through a supplied session. The models and sessions code also begin exposing the next prepared redirect request through Response.next.
The documentation theme stops loading the Hello Bar script. The change removes its external script reference from the Sphinx layout.
The development requirements update httpbin to version 0.0.6. The pin in requirements.txt replaces version 0.0.4.
The changelog now records that an invalid URL scheme raises ValueError. HISTORY.rst adds the item beside the existing note about pickling Session objects.
Requests tests can now exercise more request scenarios without external network access. The test module uses its httpbin fixture for header, redirect history, and timeout cases.
The quickstart's StringIO example now uses the Python 3-compatible import. It imports StringIO from the io module.

Multipart uploads now preserve repeated form fields with the same name. Request._encode_files accepts ordered key-value tuples for data and files, and the tests exercise multiple values alongside file uploads.
Importing Requests no longer automatically imports its async module. The package initializer removes the attempted import and exception handler.
The Makefile lint target no longer reports unused imports. It adds Flake8's F401 rule to the ignore list for Requests.
Response success checks now use Requests' HTTPError rather than urllib2's exception. The response model sets its success flag through raise_for_status and adjusts how responses are tested for truth.
Callers can now supply request hooks that modify arguments before a Request is constructed. The public request function accepts hooks and sends the argument dictionary through dispatch_hook.
The bundled urllib3 is refreshed with new connection classes and related transport changes. The connection module aliases the standard HTTP classes so it can define its own wrappers.

Expired cookies now get removed from the session jar during response handling. The Session code extracts response cookies directly into the existing jar instead of only merging a separate response jar.
Session cookie handling now has a dedicated merge helper. The new merge_session_cookies function in requests/cookies.py centralizes work used by Session requests and redirects.
The community documentation removes its sponsors page. The deleted sponsors.rst contained acknowledgments of the organizations and individuals funding Requests.
The project now uses requests.readthedocs.io as its documentation site. The new links appear in the README, contribution guide, package metadata, and documentation templates.
The documentation homepage adds a trademark symbol to the Requests tagline. The change updates the main heading in docs/index.rst.

The bundled urllib3 code updates how it prepares connections through a proxy. The package refresh also changes security warnings to display whenever they occur and touches the retry and PyOpenSSL modules.
Headers set to None on a session are now omitted from prepared requests. The merge_setting helper filters those values, and a regression test checks an unset Accept-Encoding header.
The repository moves its community policy files into .github. The code of conduct, contribution guide, and security policy are placed there, with the security text in Markdown.
The invalid URL tests now cover host-and-port strings that have no explicit HTTP scheme. RequestsTestCase checks that those strings raise InvalidSchema.
The contribution guide now links to the AI Policy at its repository location. The link in .github/CONTRIBUTING.md uses the full repository-relative path under .github.
The installation guide adds step-by-step instructions for obtaining Requests. It shows pip and easy_install commands and updates the heading for the package index mirror.
Requests adds preliminary dictionary types for storing multiple values per key. The structures module introduces MultiDict and related types with support for optional conversion on lookup.
The bundled urllib3 now requests buffered HTTP responses where Python supports them. Its connection pool falls back to the older response call, and the multipart code updates its boundary generator.
The contributor list corrects the original author's GitHub profile link. AUTHORS.rst restores the kennethreitz handle in the existing entry.
A cookie with a nonnumeric Max-Age no longer fails conversion with a value error. The morsel_to_cookie helper catches the failed numeric conversion.
The development to-do list removes work that has already been closed. The deleted entries in todo.rst include OAuth, removal of Poster, and more flexible context management.
The changelog fixes a typo in a note about Windows proxy resolution. HISTORY.md corrects the spelling of registry entries.
The README revises its introductory description of Requests' use in other tools. The update notes that the library powers tools readers may already use.
The documentation navigation now calls its development section the Contributor Guide. The change updates the heading in docs/index.rst.
The README revises the overview of existing Python HTTP libraries. The change softens the wording of the comparison in README.rst.
The quickstart's equivalent POST examples now compare the form data they submitted. This avoids depending on incidental metadata in the full httpbin responses.
A session's prefetch setting now survives pickling and is passed into new requests. Request stores the default and applies it during sending, and a test exercises an unpickled session.
The README adds the Requests sidebar logo near its title. The new image links to the documentation homepage.
Hook registration now checks the Callable interface for Python 3.1 compatibility. Request.register_hook updates both single callbacks and iterable entries, and its tests use the same check.
The Requests package moves under the src directory. The packaging configuration and Makefile update the source paths used for installation, linting, tests, and coverage.
The README's documentation address is now styled as inline code in the link label. The underlying Requests 2 documentation destination stays the same.
The changelog now records a bundled urllib3 update. HISTORY.rst lists the move to urllib3 1.16 under miscellaneous changes.
The changelog records a recursion fix in urllib2-based authentication. The HISTORY.rst update mentions Basic and Digest authentication and notes an internal refactor.
This commit tidies the URL utility constants. The unreserved character set in requests/utils.py is reformatted onto a shorter expression.
The internationalized domain name test is disabled temporarily. The change comments out RequestsTestSuite.test_idna and its URL assertion.
Requests completes its switch from charade back to chardet. The changelog explains the projects' merge, and the advanced guide and setup.py replace the remaining references.
Users can now access parsed Link headers through Response.links. The response model uses parse_header_links and also corrects the Response.json docstring.
Unsupported dependency versions now produce a warning during import. The Requests initializer checks urllib3 and chardet versions and reports a RequestsDependencyWarning.
The project adds files for building a Debian package of Requests. The debian directory introduces the package control metadata, changelog, build rules, and documentation list.
The Twitter streaming example now keeps the response body from being downloaded in advance. The advanced guide adds prefetch=False to the streaming request.
The documentation homepage wraps long prose lines at about 80 characters. The formatting change in index.rst leaves the text about Requests and urllib2 intact.
The project adds a standalone security disclosure policy. SECURITY.md tells reporters how to contact the designated maintainers privately about a potential vulnerability.
The advanced guide now shows the preferred environment variable for a custom CA bundle. Its example uses REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and lists CURL_CA_BUNDLE as a fallback.
The request settings test now expects the library's own timeout exception. RequestsTestSuite uses a small positive timeout and drops the urllib2 import.
The advanced guide corrects indentation in the Twitter streaming example. The JSON parsing line is aligned under the check that filters keep-alive lines.
The status code registry restores the older aliases for HTTP 308. Existing callers can still use resume and resume_incomplete alongside permanent_redirect.
The repository now has a CODEOWNERS file. It names the lead maintainers for deployment-related files such as workflows, version metadata, and the release history.
This commit makes a test edit to exercise a commit hook. The change is near the heading in README.rst.
The build identifier now matches Requests version 2.6.0. The package initializer corrects the __build__ value while leaving __version__ in place.
This is an empty commit. It contains no file or module changes.
Response.history remains a list even after redirects are followed. Session.send stops converting the collected history to a tuple, and the tests check the type with and without redirects.
The API reference adds documentation for the asynchronous request helpers. Its new Async section lists map and the verb functions from requests.async and replaces the old Curl section.
Requests only enables urllib3's PyOpenSSL fallback when it needs SNI support. The package initializer checks for the standard SSL module and its SNI support before applying the fallback.

Invalid response JSON now raises a consistent Requests exception. Response.json uses requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError, which retains compatibility with the underlying decoder exceptions and can also be caught as a RequestException.
Header expansion now returns string input unchanged. The header_expand helper recognizes a basestring before attempting further expansion.
The sponsors page explains why it lists major contributors. The added text in sponsors.rst describes these organizations as helping sustain Requests.
The README adds vertical spacing below the project attribution. The change inserts a paragraph containing a nonbreaking space.
The changelog adds two missing fixes. HISTORY.rst records restored SNI support and a correction for HTTP proxies that require authentication.
Requests now formally declares Python 3.15 support. The packaging metadata adds the classifier and the test workflow stops treating the 3.15 job as allowed to fail.
This commit brings much of the Requests codebase into line with PEP 8. The changes clean up argument spacing and formatting in modules such as requests.api, requests.core, and requests.models.
The Requests 2.0.1 release notes now mention the bundled dependency updates. The changelog adds a note about internal urllib3 and chardet.
The Session.max_redirects documentation now gives the default limit. The attribute comment points to DEFAULT_REDIRECT_LIMIT and states that the value is 30.
The security extra now installs a compatible PyOpenSSL version on Python 2.6. Setup.py caps the old interpreter below PyOpenSSL 18 while retaining the existing minimum version.
The pre-commit configuration now uses ruff-pre-commit version 0.15.22. The change updates the pinned hook from 0.15.21.
The Response class drops its experimental JSON line iterator. The models module removes iter_json, which had decoded each nonempty line as JSON.
The Digest streaming test changes its comparisons for compatibility with Python 3. RequestsTestCase.test_DIGEST_STREAM converts raw read results and the empty comparison value to strings.

Responses encountered during redirects now have their own history of prior responses. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects attaches a copy of the accumulated history, and a regression test checks that it is saved.
The project credits Muhammad Yasoob Ullah Khalid as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and GitHub handle under Patches and Suggestions.

The API documentation now describes separate connection and read timeouts. The change adds ConnectTimeout and ReadTimeout to the exception reference and updates the timeout descriptions used by requests and sessions.
The Windows CI job now runs the coverage target. Appveyor.yml replaces the previous make ci invocation with the coverage command.
The documentation stops showing links to page source files. Docs/conf.py disables the source-link option to work with Read the Docs.
The advanced guide fixes syntax highlighting in its multiple-file upload example. It adds the missing Python console continuation prompts to the list of file tuples.
The README adds a short invitation to read the documentation. The new heading appears after the paragraph on compatibility with PyPy.
Requests can now locate the FreeBSD system CA bundle. The certificate lookup paths in requests/utils.py include the file provided by ca_root_nss.
The release history adds an entry for Requests 2.15.1. HISTORY.rst records the release date and a brief note.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.7.2. The package initializer updates the release identifiers, and the changelog records a PATCH fix.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.10.8. The changelog records a chunked streaming fix and proxy environment support, and requests.defaults enables trust_env by default.
The project credits Peter Manser as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The vendored urllib3 dependency is bumped to 1.19.1. The refresh also updates the App Engine module to obtain urljoin from its compatibility layer.
Response hooks run at the session level without a second call from the adapter. HTTPAdapter.build_response drops its duplicate dispatch, and Session.request keeps the hook result as the response.
The documentation homepage now describes Requests downloads as a daily count. It replaces the monthly figure with a statement of over 400,000 downloads per day.
The changelog explains how Requests handles URL errors such as connection refusal and timeouts. HISTORY.rst notes that callers can surface those failures with raise_for_status.
The generic request function gets a full docstring. It describes the Response return value and explains options such as the method, URL, query parameters, body, and headers.
The Travis build now uses the Makefile to install its dependencies. The Makefile also runs the coverage command inside the Pipenv environment.
The Request model gains a read method. Request.read in requests/core.py returns the content already associated with the request.
The README changes the heading above the list of supported features. The new markup attempts to center it and uses the wording Supported Features.
Requests now validates HTTP header names as well as their values. The header validation helper uses separate rules for text and bytes, and tests cover invalid leading whitespace and line breaks.

The PreparedRequest documentation explains why calling prepare_cookies twice usually leaves the existing header in place. The method's docstring describes the underlying cookie library behavior and identifies when regenerating the header is possible.
The development guide removes its old certificate bundle instructions for downstream packagers. The change deletes the Downstream Repackaging section from todo.rst.
The test suite adds coverage for turning a request into a curl command. RequestsTestSuite checks curl_from_request for common methods, custom headers, query parameters, and authenticated requests.
The Requests package is bumped to version 2.14.2. The changelog records that revised dependency markers improve compatibility with older setuptools releases.
Coverage runs now execute the Requests tests concurrently. The Makefile's coverage target uses nine boxed pytest workers while retaining terminal and XML reports.

HTTP Basic authentication now handles credentials supplied as bytes consistently. The _basic_auth_str helper decodes username and password byte strings using Latin-1 before assembling the authorization value.
This commit fixes extra spacing in the PATCH helper. The call to request in requests/api.py now uses the usual spacing around its data argument.
Requests adds a top-level guide for people contributing changes or reporting problems. CONTRIBUTING.md directs users to the contributor guide and the project's development philosophy.
The advanced guide begins documenting transport adapters. The draft in advanced.rst also tidies formatting in the preceding prepared request examples.
The developer documentation's Authors page now includes an image. The change places the new image just below the title in authors.rst.
Streaming decompression now passes empty bytes when requesting buffered output from the decoder. The stream_decompress helper uses the compatibility bytes type in place of an empty text string.
The vendored packages initializer now exposes urllib3. The change in requests/packages/__init__.py replaces the old Poster import.
TooManyRedirects now includes the affected request and response. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects attaches them to the exception, and redirect tests check the extra context.
Requests now follows redirects with an uppercase URL scheme. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects lowercases the scheme before preparing the redirect destination.
Multipart fields now handle iterable values and Unicode more like regular form parameters. RequestEncodingMixin._encode_files skips None values and UTF-8 encodes text field names and values.
The early Requests core adds documentation for its request and authentication code. The _Request wrapper now explains that it allows the HTTP method to be set on a urllib2 request.
The community support guide starts listing PGP fingerprints for the security contacts. The change adds the fingerprint section and records the key for the maintainer identified as sigmavirus24.

Requests updates how its authentication and transport code handle text and bytes across Python versions. The compatibility module defines the relevant aliases, and requests/auth.py imports URL parsing and string types through it.
The documentation now labels sponsor placements as sponsored ads. The wording changes in the native sponsor markup in hacks.html.
Readers can now support Requests through a Flattr button in the documentation sidebar. The templates add a donation section and update the theme to support the button.
The bundled idna package now resolves imports within its own copy. Its codec and compat modules use relative imports for core and codec helpers.
This commit removes trailing whitespace across the project. The cleanup includes CI configuration, sidebar templates, and user and community documentation.
The Requests package initializer now uses explicit relative imports for its own modules. It enables absolute import semantics and imports packages and core from the current package.
The Request model now accepts and stores hooks while handling absent cookie data safely. The changes in requests/models.py also update response cookie merging and the connection reuse path.
The test suite now checks connection reuse for direct and proxied requests. A new dummy HTTP server counts connections, and the keep-alive tests use those counts.
The source distribution now includes the main Requests test script. The change adds test_requests.py to MANIFEST.in.
The test suite adds a failing case for cookies carried through redirects. RequestsTestCase.test_cookie_sent_on_redirect stores a session cookie and checks the header seen at the redirected endpoint.
The changelog expands its example for updating code that uses connection pools. HISTORY.rst fixes the code-block markup and adds an alternative based on PoolManager.

Redirects no longer lose authorization merely because the URL changes between an implicit and explicit default port. SessionRedirectMixin.should_strip_auth treats those ports as equivalent when the scheme is unchanged, and a new test checks the rule.
The project credits Steve Pulec and updates the release history. HISTORY.rst records a redundant chunked-transfer generator cleanup and a fix for Response.ok raising Timeout in safe mode.
Requests docstrings no longer emit invalid escape sequence warnings on Python 3.6. The affected API, Session, and Response methods use raw strings for their documentation.
CI workflows now declare the minimum GitHub token permissions they need. The CodeQL, lint, and test workflows use read access where possible, with a separate permission to publish CodeQL results.
The CodeQL workflow now uses github/codeql-action version 4.33.0. The change updates its initialization, autobuild, and analysis steps from version 4.32.0.

The settings context manager now accepts multiple named settings. The settings class in requests/__init__.py saves existing values, applies the requested settings, and restores the originals when the context exits.
The session header test now checks that callers can override a default header for one request. RequestsTestSuite sends a custom User-Agent through a session and verifies that the server sees it.
The project credits Om Prakash Kumar as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and GitHub handle under Patches and Suggestions.
The session API wrappers revise how they pass arguments to request helpers. Session._map_api_methods now builds an argument collection explicitly instead of merging all selected attributes at once.
The quickstart explains what happens when a response repeats a header name. Requests combines the values into one entry in the response headers mapping according to the HTTP specification.
Multipart uploads now accept file contents supplied directly as bytes. Request._encode_files wraps those values in a file-like buffer, and a new test sends a string-backed file upload.
The Requests package is bumped from version 0.3.0 to 0.3.1. The core module updates both the version and build constants.
A response restored from pickle now has a raw attribute. Response.__setstate__ sets it to None so callers can access the attribute without an AttributeError.
Editing a copied request's headers no longer edits its source request. Request.copy shallow-copies mutable fields such as headers, query parameters, cookies, and hooks before building the copy.
Filename inference now recognizes more string-like names on Python 2 and Python 3. The guess_filename helper uses the compatibility basestring type, and tests cover valid names and non-string inputs.
The contributor list adds two Twitter profile links. AUTHORS.rst links the entries for Alexander Karpinsky and Michael Becker to their accounts.
The documentation homepage updates its testimonials attribution. The entry in index.rst removes the Library of Congress and retains Twitter as the named example.
The Travis configuration removes its custom test script block. The cleanup in .travis.yml drops the explicit README check and make ci lines from that section.
Redirect responses no longer appear in their own history. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects assigns a copy of the preceding responses, and a test checks every response in a three-redirect chain.
The project credits Mikko Ohtamaa as a contributor. The AUTHORS file adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The project removes its obsolete tox test configuration. The deleted tox.ini contained the older Python environment list and JUnit reporting command.
The native string conversion helper moves to a private module to break a circular import. The cookie adapter uses requests._internal_utils, and requests.utils is updated alongside the move.
Requests now adds a Content-Length header when sending requests on this path. Request.send starts with zero and replaces it with the body length when a body is present.
Malformed Content-Type parameters are now parsed more reliably. The _parse_content_type_header helper revises its handling of parameter values, and utility tests cover parsing and encoding lookup.
The CaseInsensitiveDict documentation reverts a small formatting change. The docstring joins the plural suffix to the inline reference to lowercasing keys.
The documentation homepage now reports more than 1.5 million downloads from PyPI. The update replaces the earlier one-million figure in index.rst.
The README updates its example for registering automatic authentication. The example uses the auth_manager's add_auth method and cleans up the displayed response attribute names.
Redirected requests now retain the timeout configured on the original call. Request._build_response passes the timeout to the request it creates for the next hop.
The early Request model now requires uppercase HTTP verb names. Its validation and send logic compare directly against uppercase method names.
Line-by-line response iteration no longer drops the final line when it lacks a newline. Response.iter_lines yields the remaining fragment after the stream ends, and a regression test checks the case.
The documentation homepage adds a programming quiz link for people seeking jobs. The new text replaces the earlier direct support link and describes the associated donation.
The Request model now calls its cookie argument and attribute cookies. The change in requests/models.py updates initialization, the opener, and the request and redirect paths to use that name.
The documentation sidebar renames its newsletter section to Stay Informed. The change updates the heading in both sidebar templates.
The README now calls the HTTP methods on the requests module in its usage examples. The update corrects the module name used by examples such as GET, HEAD, and PUT.
The quickstart now demonstrates Requests' built-in OAuth support. Its OAuth section replaces a link to an external add-on with an OAuth1 example using requests.auth.
The README switches its build status badge to the Requests trunk job. The badge image and link replace the previous Travis CI references.
The pre-commit configuration now uses ruff-pre-commit version 0.15.20. The change updates the hook revision from 0.15.18.
Multipart form values now use the compatibility string conversion. RequestEncodingMixin._encode_files switches from builtin_str to the compatibility str alias.
Multipart file data is now encoded when the request is created. The Request initializer uses _encode_files to retain the prepared body, addressing file uploads that failed with Digest authentication.
The packaging script now reads the version source as UTF-8. Setup.py adds the encoding when opening requests/__init__.py to fix the CI packaging step.
The adapter now determines whether a proxied request uses HTTPS by parsing the URL's scheme. HTTPAdapter.request_url uses that result when choosing the form of the outgoing request target.
The Session documentation now describes the cookie jar stored on the session. It explains that RequestsCookieJar is the default and that other CookieJar implementations are accepted.
The package docstring now introduces the Requests HTTP library with a basic GET example. Requests/__init__.py shows how to make a request and inspect its response status.

Multipart uploads now accept non-string values in regular form fields. RequestEncodingMixin._encode_files converts those values to text while preserving bytes, and a test sends a numeric value alongside a file.
Multipart request preparation restores the earlier order for processing form fields. Request._encode_files moves the loop that appends converted data values earlier in the encoding method.
Requests now accepts idna version 2.6. Setup.py raises the upper bound to versions below 2.7, and HISTORY.rst records the new supported version.
The repository now ignores reports generated by Jenkins jobs. The .gitignore changes cover the coverage, nose, and pylint output files.

Redirect URLs now retain the previous fragment when the new location has none. SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects tracks the fragment across hops, and tests check that fragments stay out of the HTTP request itself.
The advanced guide formats the name of the OpenSSL c_rehash utility as code. The change is in the certificate verification instructions.
The installation guide now leads with a simpler Pip Install section. It shows a single installation command and points readers without pip to a Python installation guide.
Code blocks have more room on mobile in the documentation. The hacks.html template lets preformatted examples extend into the right margin.
The contribution guide updates its link to Sphinx. The reference in contributing.rst now uses the current HTTPS documentation address.
OAuth authentication now imports its helpers directly from OAuthLib. Requests/auth.py drops the obsolete private wrapper and imports the common and OAuth1 helpers from their source modules.

The Requests code of conduct now refers to the Python Community Code of Conduct. The policy describes expectations for project participation, and the contributor guide also refreshes its related link.
The project credits James Clarke as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name and handle under Patches and Suggestions.
The documentation theme stops styling scrollbars. The Flasky stylesheet removes its custom WebKit scrollbar rules.

Session headers now use a more complete case-insensitive mapping. CaseInsensitiveDict implements MutableMapping, remembers the last spelling of a key, and still lets callers look up names regardless of case.
An invalid response now returns None when callers read its content. Response.content catches the missing raw response, and a regression test exercises a failed request.
A failed new connection is no longer reported as a connection timeout. HTTPAdapter.send distinguishes urllib3's NewConnectionError from timeout errors when translating the failure.

The redirect code now explains which request is used to extract cookies. The comment in SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects documents why extraction uses the original request before the prepared copy is changed.
An explicit verification setting on a request now takes precedence over the session default. Session.request uses its default only when verify is None, so a caller can pass False.

Requests now preserves quoted slashes when preparing request and redirect paths. The Request model uses the requote_path helper to normalize paths instead of applying the old unquote and quote sequence directly.
The source distribution manifest corrects its test file pattern. MANIFEST.in now uses the intended wildcard for files under tests.
The changelog adds release notes for Requests 2.14.1. HISTORY.rst records a dependency marker change that improves compatibility with older versions of pip.
The test suite now verifies that cookies set on a session are sent with its requests. RequestsTestSuite compares the cookies echoed by the server with the values given to the session.
The documentation theme now shows a GitHub banner for Requests. Docs/conf.py sets the GitHub owner and repository in the theme options.

JSON decoding errors now preserve their formatted message and decoder details. The Requests JSONDecodeError initializer constructs the decoder exception before initializing the IOError base, and tests check that the document attribute survives.
The Makefile removes an old Pyflakes file selection rule. The cleanup drops the explicit list expression and its comments about excluding documentation, tests, and virtual environments.
The documentation homepage fixes the spelling of maintenance mode. The correction is in the note describing the status of Requests 2.x.

Requests now loads its IDNA dependency only when preparing an internationalized hostname. PreparedRequest moves the import into _get_idna_encoded_host and provides a fallback for an unavailable vendored import.
Windows CI now includes a Python 3.6 job. The AppVeyor matrix adds a 64-bit interpreter and selects the py36 tox environment.

Requests now calculates Content-Length from the unread portion of a seekable body. PreparedRequest.prepare_content_length subtracts the starting position from the end and restores that position before sending.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.13.2. The changelog highlights no required dependencies, Response.reason, OAuth query signing, and fixes for client certificates and openSUSE.
The README fixes a spelling mistake in the line following the installation example. The word guaranteed is now spelled correctly.
The project credits Marty Alchin as a contributor. AUTHORS.rst adds the name under Patches and Suggestions.
The Requests package is bumped to version 0.13.6. HISTORY.rst highlights a fix for hanging connections and records the packaging fix from 0.13.5.
Requests now prefers cchardet for character detection when it is installed. The compatibility module falls back to the bundled chardet if that import is unavailable.

Normalizing a URI no longer changes the meaning of its reserved characters. The requote_path helper decodes only escapes for unreserved characters and then quotes illegal characters while preserving the reserved ones.

The authentication docs now spell out which credentials win when several sources are supplied. They explain that explicit auth takes precedence over .netrc, which in turn overrides an Authorization header set through headers.
The README simplifies its description of sending HTTP requests. It retains examples of the work Requests handles for callers, such as query strings and form encoding.
The test for closing an unread session response now uses the intended boolean assertions. RequestsTestCase checks that the content remains unconsumed and the underlying response is closed.
The packaging script fixes a missing separator in the package list. Setup.py adds a comma after the requests.packages.chardet entry.

Iterating a streamed response again now raises an explicit error if its content was already consumed without being cached. Response.iter_content keeps its ability to iterate over cached response bytes.
Requests adds a property for decoding a response as JSON. Response.json tries the decoded text or body bytes, and the models module imports the JSON decoder.
The changelog now notes that multipart uploads can omit files whose value is None. HISTORY.rst records that this input no longer raises an exception.
This is an empty commit. It contains no file or module changes.

Requests no longer sends a Cookie header when the cookie jar produces no header value. Request.send checks for None before writing the header, and a regression test verifies that the server receives no Cookie header.
The repository now ignores local IDE project settings. The change adds the .idea entry to .gitignore.
